_comment: GENERATED from the defineTool registry by scripts/gen-tool-catalog.ts — do not hand-edit. Run `npm run gen:tool-catalog` after adding/changing a tool. The compact, CI-gated projection of the tool + route surface (docs-and-memory-as-projections D-002).

tools.name: actions:recent
tools.description: List recent long-running user-initiated actions for a harness (replan, cleanup, snapshot).

guidance.when: User asks "what have I been doing?", "recent actions". Read-only feed from the actions log.
guidance.notWhen: For workspace-wide audit (cross-harness), use `cross_harness:recent_activity` or `audit:list`.

tools.name: activity:recent
tools.description: Read recent worker-activity rows (native tool calls / lifecycle / todos) from the cross-CLI activity bridge. Filter by owner (one worker's pane), harness, agent (claude/codex/omp), kind (tool/lifecycle/todos); since_id returns only rows newer than a cursor. The curator + fleet view read this; the live push is /api/activity/stream.

guidance.when: You want to inspect what a worker (or the whole fleet) has been doing — the recent native tool-call stream, todo snapshots, or lifecycle transitions. Pass owner to scope to one pane, harness to scope to one project, since_id to page forward.
guidance.notWhen: For a LIVE feed subscribe to the /api/activity/stream SSE (the pui does this). To report activity (you almost never need to) use `activity:report`. For coord messages use `coord:inbox`.

tools.name: activity:report
tools.description: Report one worker-activity event (a native tool call, lifecycle transition, or todo snapshot) to the cross-CLI activity bridge sink (harness_shared.agent_activity). Called by the per-CLI hooks on every tool call; feeds the pui fleet view + curator. The display summary is derived server-side from tool_name+tool_input when not supplied. Fire-and-forget: returns { ok, id } and never blocks.

guidance.when: Almost never call this by hand — the per-CLI hooks (posttooluse-activity-report.sh / the OMP coord-hook port) call it automatically to mirror each worker's native tool stream into the fleet view. Call directly only to inject a synthetic activity marker (e.g. a custom lifecycle note).
guidance.notWhen: To READ the activity stream use `activity:recent` (or the /api/activity/stream SSE). To coordinate with peers use `coord:send`. To drive a pui use `tui:dispatch`.

tools.name: agent_chats:archive
tools.description: Archive (soft-delete) a chat session by id.

guidance.when: User says "close that chat", "archive the X conversation" — moves the chat to archived status so it stops appearing in active lists.
guidance.notWhen: For DELETING a chat, this isn't it — archive is reversible. For UI dismissing without changing state, ignore the request and the user can do it themselves.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `agent_chats:list` first if you need to confirm the chatId.

tools.name: agent_chats:chat
tools.description: Single-turn streaming chat against an already-assembled role prompt. Returns final text + token/cost rollup; the caller is expected to persist the assistant turn.

tools.name: agent_chats:create
tools.description: Open a new chat session for a role in a harness; optionally bind it to a feature_id.

guidance.when: User says "ask the architect to ...", "have the worker do ...", or you're routing a request to a role-scoped agent. Step 1 of the two-step dispatch flow.
guidance.notWhen: For replying in the user's direct chat, just speak — don't spin up a new agent chat. For talking to ANOTHER user, use `messages:send`. For spawning a one-shot agent process (not a long-running chat), use `<spawn>` / `orchestrator.spawn`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `agent_chats:send_message` immediately (step 2 of the dispatch flow), then `ui:dispatch` with `/harness/<slug>?chat=<chatId>` so the user can watch the conversation.

tools.name: agent_chats:get
tools.description: Read one chat by id (transcript, totals, feature_lock state).

guidance.when: User names a specific chat ("the architect conversation about auth") and wants the full transcript or feature_lock state.
guidance.notWhen: For a list of chats in a harness, use `agent_chats:list` first to find the id. Don't fetch full transcripts speculatively.
guidance.chaining: Follow `agent_chats:list` to find the id.

tools.name: agent_chats:list
tools.description: List multi-turn chat sessions for a harness slug (active by default; pass includeArchived=true to see all).

guidance.when: User asks "what chats have I had with X?", "show me the conversations on sheets", or you need a chatId before resuming via ui:dispatch.
guidance.notWhen: For agents (who exists), use `agents:list`. For the transcript of a SPECIFIC chat, use `agent_chats:get`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `agent_chats:get` for detail on one chat, or `ui:dispatch` with `/harness/<slug>?chat=<chatId>` to take the user to it.

tools.name: agent_chats:send_message
tools.description: Append a user message to an existing agent chat. The harness streams the assistant reply via SSE; this tool returns as soon as the message is accepted. Pair with agent_chats:create to start a new conversation.

guidance.when: Step 2 of the dispatch flow — you just called `agent_chats:create` and need to post the user's first message to kick off the conversation. Also for follow-up messages on an existing chat the user named.
guidance.notWhen: For broadcasting to multiple recipients (inbox-style), use `messages:send`. For the user's own chat with you, just speak.
guidance.chaining: Follow `agent_chats:create` (or `agent_chats:list` if resuming). Then `ui:dispatch` to take the user to the chat.

tools.name: agent_tools:list
tools.description: List MCP-exposed tools with permission status for the caller. Each entry includes name, description, capability, roles allowlist, an `allowed` flag with `reason` when blocked, AND per-tool `guidance` (when/notWhen/chaining resolved for the queried role). Use to discover what you can call without trial-and-error.

guidance.when: Your tools playbook didn't cover a user request and you need to discover what's callable. Returns the full catalog filtered by your role, with each tool's guidance — treat this as the runtime fallback playbook.
guidance.notWhen: Don't use as a fishing expedition. If your playbook covers it, just call the tool. `agent_tools:list` costs a tool call.

tools.name: agents:list
tools.description: List agents across the workspace (optionally filtered by harness slug). Limit clamped 1..100, default 40.

guidance.when: User asks "which agents are working on X?", "what crew does sheets have?", or you need to pick the most-active matching role before calling agent_chats:create.
guidance.notWhen: For active CHAT sessions, use `agent_chats:list`. agents:list is who-exists; agent_chats:list is what-conversations.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `agent_chats:create` once you've picked the role to dispatch to.

tools.name: architect:chat
tools.description: Architect-mode chat turn: clarify spec, propose patches. Streams deltas; returns the assembled final text.

tools.name: artifacts:append
tools.description: Append to a PG-canonical text artifact (harness_text_artifacts). Creates the row if absent.

guidance.when: Add to an existing artifact without losing prior content — running notes, ongoing log, accumulating findings.
guidance.notWhen: For replacing the whole file, use `artifacts:save`. For ephemeral within-turn notes, just hold them in your reply.

tools.name: artifacts:delete
tools.description: Delete a PG-canonical text artifact row by (harness_slug, rel_path). Restricted to architect/operator/curator roles.

guidance.when: Remove an artifact that's no longer relevant. Restricted to architect/operator/curator roles by `roles` allowlist.
guidance.notWhen: Don't delete to "clean up" speculatively — artifacts cost nothing to keep, and other agents may rely on them.

tools.name: artifacts:load
tools.description: Read a PG-canonical text artifact (harness_text_artifacts) by (harness_slug, rel_path).

guidance.when: You need to read a file the harness wrote earlier (notes, intermediate outputs, plans) by its harness_slug + rel_path.
guidance.notWhen: For SOURCE CODE in the user's repo, use the filesystem tools / gitnexus. Artifacts are harness-scoped PG-canonical text only.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `artifacts:save` to round-trip, `artifacts:append` to add to an existing one.

tools.name: artifacts:save
tools.description: Upsert a PG-canonical text artifact (harness_text_artifacts) by (harness_slug, rel_path). Replaces existing content.

guidance.when: Persist a generated text artifact for later reads by other agents or future turns. Replaces existing content at the same (harness_slug, rel_path).
guidance.notWhen: For appending to an existing file, use `artifacts:append` — save fully replaces. For source code, write to the repo via filesystem tools, not artifacts.

tools.name: audit:list
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what happened recently?", "who did X?", or you need a forensic timeline of agent + user actions.

When NOT to use: For ACTIVE / in-flight work, use `harness:status` or `actions:recent`. Audit is a write-log, not a live view.

guidance.when: User asks "what happened recently?", "who did X?", or you need a forensic timeline of agent + user actions.
guidance.notWhen: For ACTIVE / in-flight work, use `harness:status` or `actions:recent`. Audit is a write-log, not a live view.

tools.name: autoloop:control
tools.description: Pause/resume a harness's blueprint-scheduled autoloop (flips its bp-schedule-* routine rows — durable) or reset its error circuit (zeroes consecutive_errors so backoff stops withholding fires).

guidance.when: User says "pause the autoloop", "turn autopilot back on", or a circuit-open harness needs its error counter reset after a fix. Per-harness, durable.
guidance.notWhen: For PAUSING all of the operator (silence-mode-style), use the operator-pause flag — autoloop is per-harness. For pausing git-sync or another non-schedule routine, flip that routine directly.
guidance.chaining: autoloop:status first to see the schedule routines + circuit state; reset-errors after fixing whatever made the fires fail.

tools.name: autoloop:status
tools.description: Read autoloop_state rows (last_fired_at, last_status, consecutive_errors) for a harness slug.

guidance.when: User asks "is the autoloop running?", "is the harness on autopilot?". Reads enabled/paused state + recent tick info.
guidance.notWhen: For TURNING the autoloop on/off, use `autoloop:control`. For harness liveness in general, use `harness:health`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `autoloop:control` if the user wants to change state.

tools.name: backup:diff
tools.description: Diff two kopia snapshots — list files added/changed/removed.

guidance.when: Diff current state vs a backup snapshot — what would change if we restored. Read-only.
guidance.notWhen: For applying the diff, use `backup:restore`. diff is the dry-run view.

tools.name: backup:promote
tools.description: Promote a restored clone to live by atomic rename. Live dir becomes .broken-<ts>-<name>/. Reversible by renaming back. Auto-snapshots before promotion as belt-and-suspenders.

guidance.when: Promote a backup to active (roll forward to it without rolling back). Used after testing a restore.
guidance.notWhen: For UNDOING to an earlier state, use `backup:rollback`. promote moves forward; rollback moves back.

tools.name: backup:restore
tools.description: Restore a kopia snapshot. mode="clone" (default) writes to .restored/<id>/ and never overwrites live state; mode="in_place" overwrites the target after taking a safety snapshot first.

guidance.when: Restore a backup snapshot — replay PG dump + filesystem into the workspace. Destructive: replaces current state.
guidance.notWhen: For ROLLING BACK without changing the snapshot list, use `backup:rollback`. restore is the full apply.

tools.name: backup:rollback
tools.description: Undo a previous backup:promote. Renames the .broken-<ts>-<name>/ dir back to live; current live becomes .rolled-back-<ts>-<name>/.

guidance.when: Roll back to the immediately-prior backup. Reversible only by re-applying via restore.
guidance.notWhen: For applying a SPECIFIC backup, use `backup:restore` with the id.

tools.name: backup:settings_get
tools.description: Read backup settings + repo stats for the active workspace.

guidance.when: Read backup configuration — schedule, retention, destinations.
guidance.notWhen: For runtime BACKUP state (last run, next run), check the destinations directly.

tools.name: backup:settings_set
tools.description: Patch backup settings for the active workspace. All fields optional; missing keys preserve existing values.

guidance.when: Update backup configuration. Confirm the change out loud first — affects automated backups going forward.
guidance.notWhen: For one-shot backup creation, use `backup:snapshot_create`. settings_set is for the schedule/policy.

tools.name: backup:snapshot_create
tools.description: Create a kopia snapshot of the active workspace before a destructive op. Returns the snapshot id so the same agent can restore from it if needed.

guidance.when: Create a new backup snapshot of the workspace. Use before risky migrations or major state changes.
guidance.notWhen: For routine commits, this isn't needed — backup snapshots are heavyweight (whole-workspace). For per-harness portable snapshots, use the snapshots tools instead.

tools.name: backup:snapshot_list
tools.description: List recent kopia snapshots for the active workspace.

guidance.when: List backup snapshots — point-in-time captures of the workspace's PG + filesystem state.
guidance.notWhen: For HARNESS snapshots (portable artifacts you can publish), use `snapshots:list`. backup:snapshot_list is the full-workspace recovery view.

tools.name: blueprint:catalog
tools.description: List the blueprints available to instantiate — built-in + Cupboard-installed (installed shadows built-in, like the extends resolver). Each entry summarizes the shape: id, tier, version, description, workItem kind, decider + roles, spine model (decider-edges vs program-steps), triggers, dispatch policy (when declared), requiresRepo, and whether it is a one-shot launch blueprint (fired via system:blueprint-run) vs a harness pipeline (instantiated via harness:create). Broken entries are kept as {id, tier, error}.

guidance.when: Deciding WHICH blueprint shape fits a piece of work before creating a harness — the Pot operator's first stop (decomposable features → coding, investigation → research, parallel codemod → migration, a decision → vote/deliberate). Also the discovery surface for what launch blueprints exist.
guidance.notWhen: Deep-inspecting one blueprint (validation errors/warnings) — blueprint:validate {id}. Authoring — blueprint:create/extend.
guidance.chaining: blueprint:catalog → blueprint:validate {id} → harness:create {blueprintId} (pipelines) or fire the launchable ones via their trigger/system:blueprint-run.

tools.name: blueprint:create
tools.description: Author a NEW Harness Blueprint from a blueprint object. Validates it (schema + semantics) and returns {ok, errors, warnings, yaml} — the canonical YAML to persist at .papercusp/blueprint.yaml. Does not write files or create a harness. For a blueprint that inherits, use blueprint:extend.

guidance.when: Authoring a brand-new blueprint shape from scratch (rare — usually you extend `coding`/`base`/`research`). Returns validated canonical YAML.
guidance.notWhen: Inheriting from an existing blueprint — use blueprint:extend (cheaper, less to author). Creating the harness itself — harness:create.
guidance.chaining: blueprint:create → (inspect yaml) → harness:create { blueprint } or write .papercusp/blueprint.yaml.

tools.name: blueprint:extend
tools.description: Author a CHILD blueprint extending a parent (e.g. extend "coding"). You supply only the overrides; the tool merges onto the parent, validates the resolved result, and returns {ok, errors, warnings, yaml} — the small child override file for .papercusp/blueprint.yaml. The parent resolves installed (~/.papercusp/blueprints, e.g. Cupboard-installed) → built-in.

guidance.when: The usual way to make a new blueprint: inherit shared structure from any resolvable parent (a built-in, or a Cupboard-installed blueprint) and override only what differs (knobs, a few roles, a spine tweak). Cheap to author.
guidance.notWhen: Authoring a wholly new shape with no parent — blueprint:create.
guidance.chaining: blueprint:extend { parent:"coding", overrides } → (inspect yaml) → harness:create { blueprint }.

tools.name: blueprint:validate
tools.description: Validate a Harness Blueprint — a blueprint id (resolved installed → built-in, e.g. "coding" or a Cupboard-installed id) OR inline YAML/JSON. Returns {ok, errors, warnings, summary} (errors/warnings instead of throwing) so you can iterate. Checks the Zod schema + reachability/termination/guards/bounded-recursion.

guidance.when: Before persisting a blueprint you authored (with blueprint:create/extend) or to inspect a built-in. Always validate before writing .papercusp/blueprint.yaml or calling harness:create.
guidance.notWhen: To run a blueprint — that is the orchestrator. To create a harness — harness:create.
guidance.chaining: blueprint:create/extend → blueprint:validate → (write .papercusp/blueprint.yaml or harness:create).

tools.name: brainstorm:chat
tools.description: Brainstorm partner chat turn: expand ideas, suggest analogues, challenge assumptions. Streams deltas; returns the assembled final text.

tools.name: chat:ask_choice
tools.description: Present the user with a structured set of clickable choices and BLOCK until they pick. The tool returns the chosen option(s) (or {declined:true} if the user skipped). Use for yes/no, accept/reject, or pick-one-of questions with up to 6 options. Set multi:true for "select all that apply".

guidance.when: You need a yes/no, accept/reject, or pick-one-of decision from the user before continuing. Renders clickable buttons in the chat; the tool returns the choice as its result. You can keep working in the same turn after the result lands.
guidance.notWhen: For OPEN-ENDED questions ("describe what you want", "paste the error"), keep using plain text. Use 2-3 options; 4+ only when genuinely distinct (6 hard max).

tools.name: conversations:answer
tools.description: Answer a question conversation. Appends an answer to its thread and notifies subscribers (the asker gets it in their inbox). The asker/resolver accepts an answer with conversations:resolve.

guidance.when: You can answer an open question (you saw it via a topic subscription or conversations:list). Post the answer here so the asker is notified and the answer is captured on resolve.
guidance.notWhen: For a non-answer comment/clarification, use conversations:post. To accept your own/another answer and close the question, use conversations:resolve.
guidance.chaining: conversations:answer → the asker conversations:resolve (accepts it, captures it to the knowledge layer for the next asker).

tools.name: conversations:get
tools.description: Read one conversation in full: the seed, topic tags, the whole thread (posts oldest-first), the accepted answer if resolved, and follower count.

guidance.when: You have a conversation_id (from coord:ask, conversations:list, or an inbox notice) and want the full thread.
guidance.notWhen: Browsing many → conversations:list.
guidance.chaining: conversations:get → conversations:answer / conversations:post / conversations:join / conversations:resolve.

tools.name: conversations:join
tools.description: Follow a single conversation so its updates are injected into your inbox. mode = full | digest | mention (D-006). Idempotent — re-joining updates the mode/TTL. Pass leave:true to stop following.

guidance.when: A specific conversation is one you want to track or contribute to. Posting/answering auto-joins you; call this to follow without posting, or to change your delivery mode.
guidance.notWhen: To follow an AREA (not one thread), use topics:subscribe. For a one-time read, just conversations:get.
guidance.chaining: conversations:list / conversations:get → conversations:join.

tools.name: conversations:list
tools.description: List conversations (questions + discussions), newest first. Filter by kind, state (open|resolved|closed), harness, and topic. Each row carries its topic tags; conversations:get for the full thread.

guidance.when: Browsing for open questions you could answer, or finding a conversation by topic/harness. For updates pushed to you, subscribe to a topic instead.
guidance.notWhen: You already have a conversation_id → conversations:get.
guidance.chaining: conversations:list → conversations:get → conversations:answer / conversations:join.

tools.name: conversations:post
tools.description: Start a discussion (open-ended) or append a reply to an existing conversation. Omit conversation_id to start a new discussion tagged with topics; pass conversation_id to reply. Replies fan out to the conversation's subscribers.

guidance.when: Open-ended coordination with no single answer ("how should we approach X?"), or contributing to an existing thread. For a question that wants an answer, use coord:ask instead.
guidance.notWhen: A factual question → coord:ask (it tries knowledge first). To accept an answer + close a question → conversations:resolve.
guidance.chaining: conversations:post (start) → others conversations:post (reply) / conversations:join. conversations:get to read the thread.

tools.name: conversations:promote
tools.description: Promote a conversation (question/discussion) into an engineer issue, carrying its thread. Mints an engineer_issues row (with the conversation's topics + scope), closes the conversation, and records the issue id. Use when a discussion concludes there is a real problem to track.

guidance.when: A conversation has concluded that there is a concrete, trackable problem — turn it into an issue so it can be claimed, prioritized, and promoted to a feature.
guidance.notWhen: A question that just needs an answer → conversations:resolve (captures the answer). An open discussion still in progress → leave it. To file a fresh issue unrelated to a conversation → issues:create.
guidance.chaining: conversations:get → conversations:promote → issues:get / issues:claim. The issue keeps the conversation's thread; further discussion uses issues:comment.

tools.name: conversations:resolve
tools.description: Resolve a question: accept an answer (by text or by accepted_post_id) and close it. The accepted answer is captured to the knowledge layer (mem0 by default) so the next coord:ask finds it synchronously. Notifies subscribers.

guidance.when: A question conversation has been answered satisfactorily. Accept the best answer here — this both closes it and feeds the answer back so nobody has to ask again.
guidance.notWhen: Still gathering answers → leave it open. For an open-ended discussion that just ran its course, this still works (capture is skippable with capture:none).
guidance.chaining: conversations:answer → conversations:resolve { accepted_post_id }. Provide accepted_answer to write a synthesized answer instead of quoting a single post.

tools.name: coord:ack
tools.description: Acknowledge a coord message by its msg_id. Posts a `kind: "ack"` entry in your outbox addressed back at the original sender, so they can see you received it.

guidance.when: After acting on (or deliberately not acting on) a coord message — closes the loop for the sender.
guidance.notWhen: For routine read-and-forget. Acks are most useful for hand-offs and questions where the sender is waiting.

tools.name: coord:ask
tools.description: Ask a question knowledge-FIRST. Runs search:semantic + mem0 before interrupting anyone: a hit returns answer candidates inline (with sources); a miss opens a `question` conversation routed to topic subscribers and returns immediately (answers arrive in your inbox — never blocks). Pass topics to route a miss; force_open:true to ask peers even when knowledge had candidates.

guidance.when: You have a question and want the fastest correct answer without needlessly interrupting a peer. Always include topics so a miss reaches the right people. For a harness-specific question pass harness.
guidance.notWhen: For an open-ended discussion (no single answer), use conversations:post. To turn-block on a peer/human, use coord:escalate / coord:handoff instead — coord:ask is deliberately non-blocking.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → coord:ask (with topics). On a miss you get a conversation_id; conversations:get to read replies, conversations:resolve when answered.

tools.name: coord:ask-owner
tools.description: Ask the OWNER (the human) a question and wait a bounded time for an answer (opens a question thread + lands it in the human inbox). Returns { answered, answer }. For asking PEERS knowledge-first, use coord:ask instead.

guidance.when: You need the owner's (human's) input on a decision and can wait briefly, but want to proceed (e.g. fall through to a vote) if they don't respond in time.
guidance.notWhen: A peer question or a knowledge lookup — use coord:ask (knowledge-first: searches existing knowledge, then routes to topic subscribers). A blocking decision that MUST have a human answer — use coord:escalate (severity: blocker).

tools.name: coord:await-inbox
tools.description: Idle end-of-turn scaffold: register a STANDING wake watch on YOUR OWN inbox so a later coord:send {wake:true} to you re-invokes you, then end your turn (sleep). Call this exactly when your work-list is drained / you are awaiting direction — not while you still have work. Sugar over watch:create on your inbox-wake key (the deliver-and-wake rendezvous). Returns the watch id + your inbox-wake key.

guidance.when: You are idle at end-of-turn — work-list empty or blocked, awaiting the Queen / a peer to send you something. Register the watch, then END YOUR TURN. You are re-invoked when work/direction arrives via coord:send {wake:true}.
guidance.notWhen: You still have queued work — keep going. A specific one-shot readiness (a lock grant, a peer's artifact) — use events:await on that exact key. A sub-minute wait inside one turn — just block.
guidance.chaining: coord:await-inbox → end your turn. On wake the turn text carries the message that woke you (read coord:inbox for the full set). To stop watching: events:cancel.

tools.name: coord:declare-intent
tools.description: Declare what you are working on right now — a one-line intent, optionally the plan slug and the files in scope. Other agents see this via coord:presence. Declares your whole current state; omitted fields reset.

guidance.when: Starting a distinct piece of work, so other agents see what you have taken on.
guidance.notWhen: Every turn — the OMP hook heartbeats automatically; call this when your intent changes.

tools.name: coord:deliberate
tools.description: Run the uncertainty ladder on a decision: ask the owner first → if unresolved, run a vote → if the vote is split, escalate a curated summary. The full escalate-only-when-needed flow.

guidance.when: A consequential decision where the owner might already have an answer, but you want an automatic fallback to a vote and a curated escalation rather than blocking.
guidance.notWhen: You already know the owner has no opinion (go straight to coord:vote) or the choice is trivial (just decide).

tools.name: coord:emit
tools.description: Emit a structured LIFECYCLE coordination notification (completion / claim / window / handoff / finding). The system fires this automatically from lifecycle events; agents rarely call it directly — use coord:send for unpredictable, contextual messages.

guidance.when: Almost never directly — the event-reaction rules fire coord:emit automatically when a work_item completes/claims, a coordination-window opens/closes, etc. Call it by hand ONLY to emit a recognized-shape lifecycle event the rules do not yet cover.
guidance.notWhen: For a genuinely contextual message (a finding's nuance, a design call, a question, a hand-written status), use coord:send — that is the unpredictable residual coord:emit deliberately does NOT carry.
guidance.chaining: The lifecycle rules render the payload via the coord-lifecycle render layer, then fire this. Pair with coord:inbox to see emitted lifecycle.

tools.name: coord:escalate
tools.description: Raise an escalation to the human. Provide severity (blocker | question | advisory), a one-line summary, and optionally a body and a small list of choice options to make resolution one click.

guidance.when: A decision you should not make alone, a blocker that requires human input, or a risky operation that needs explicit confirmation.
guidance.notWhen: Routine status updates — use coord:send. File contention — locks:queue already names the holder.

tools.name: coord:escalations
tools.description: List escalations addressed to the human. Default: all. Filter by status=open (resolved is null) or status=resolved (resolved is set).

guidance.when: Showing the human inbox; diagnostics; checking your own past escalations.
guidance.notWhen: A specific msg_id you already have — there is no escalation read-by-id tool yet; coord:escalations + filter is enough at current volumes.

tools.name: coord:feed
tools.description: Read the COMPLETE coordination stream across every agent and channel — messages, acks, notifies, broadcasts, handoffs, escalations, resolutions, plan events — newest-first with a next-page cursor. Filter by kinds, owner (matches sender OR recipient; broadcasts match any owner), plan_slug, free-text `q` (over summary/body/from/to), and a since_ts/before_ts time window. before_ts is the pagination cursor (pass back the returned `nextCursor`). Returns `{ count, total, by_kind, next_cursor, rows }`; each row is the raw envelope plus `surface` (messages|escalations|handoffs|plan-events) and a derived `broadcast` flag.

guidance.when: You need the full fleet-wide coordination timeline — auditing what agents said to each other, tracing a broadcast/handoff/escalation chain, or backing an observer UI. The all-traffic counterpart to the per-owner coord:inbox.
guidance.notWhen: For YOUR addressed messages use coord:inbox; for open human escalations use coord:escalations; for live "who is active" use coord:presence. coord:feed is the read-everything firehose, not a working inbox.

tools.name: coord:handoff
tools.description: Record a work transition. Either OPEN a new handoff to other agents (provide `to[]`, `plan_slug`, `summary`, etc.) OR ACCEPT an existing one by passing `accept_msg_id` alone.

guidance.when: Wrapping up your piece of a plan and naming who picks up next — or accepting a handoff someone made to you.
guidance.notWhen: A routine status update — use coord:send. A blocking decision — use coord:escalate.

tools.name: coord:handoffs
tools.description: List handoff records, each annotated with its acceptance file if one exists. Optional `status` filters to open (no acceptance) or accepted.

guidance.when: Diagnostics — "who handed what to whom?" or "what handoffs to me are still open?".
guidance.notWhen: A single known msg_id — there is no read-by-id tool yet; the listing is small.

tools.name: coord:inbox
tools.description: Read your coordination inbox — messages, acks, handoffs etc. addressed to you (or broadcast). Returns a summary header (counts by kind) + the most-recent `limit` entries (default 50). Ambient system broadcasts (service-health, rate-limit pauses) are excluded by default — pass include_ambient to see them. `since_ts` filters strictly later than the given ISO timestamp; `kinds` narrows to specific entry kinds.

guidance.when: At turn start (the OMP hook will do this for you once it ships); whenever you suspect another agent contacted you.
guidance.notWhen: For agent-presence ("who is active?") — use coord:presence. For file locks — use locks:queue.

tools.name: coord:message-agent
tools.description: Open a work-item-scoped conversation with a specific agent — the inbox's "Message owner" action. Creates a browseable discussion thread (Brief 25's conversations tab) scoped to the item's harness, subscribes the owning agent, and pings them so they reply in-thread. Returns { conversation_id, thread_id }.

guidance.when: You (or the human via the inbox) want to message the agent that owns a specific work-item — start a durable, scoped thread with them about that item.
guidance.notWhen: A quick one-off note to a peer with no thread — use coord:send. A question to the OWNER/human — coord:ask-owner. A reply in an existing conversation — conversations:post.
guidance.chaining: coord:message-agent → conversations:get to read the thread → conversations:post to reply.

tools.name: coord:plan-events
tools.description: Read the plan-event history — created / now_updated / decision_added / item_added / item_status_changed / promoted events across all plans. Optional `since_ts` returns only events strictly later than that ISO timestamp; `plan_slug` narrows to one plan. Distinct from coord:inbox (which scans messages, not plan-events).

guidance.when: Turn start — the OMP coordination extension calls this to show which plans changed since the agent last read. Also ad-hoc, to review recent plan activity.
guidance.notWhen: For messages / notifies / handoffs addressed to you — use coord:inbox.

tools.name: coord:presence
tools.description: List ACTIVE coordination agents (fresh heartbeat) and their declared intent. Stale sessions (heartbeat >10 min — almost certainly ended) are summarised, not listed, unless you pass include_stale. Optionally filter by workspace.

guidance.when: "Who else is working right now, and on what?" — before starting work that might overlap.
guidance.notWhen: Checking whether a specific file is free — use locks:queue for that.

tools.name: coord:resolve
tools.description: Resolve an escalation by msg_id. Records the chosen option id (or arbitrary string) and optional note as an append-only escalation_resolved event.

guidance.when: The human (or an authorised agent acting on their behalf) has decided how to proceed on an open escalation.
guidance.notWhen: Acknowledging without deciding — use coord:ack. The escalation file is the human-resolution surface.

tools.name: coord:send
tools.description: Send a message to other coordination agents. `to` is a list of ownerIds; use ["*"] to broadcast, ["human"] to surface to the user. By default the message is INJECTED (lands in the recipient's inbox, seen on their next natural turn — cheap, no token cost). Pass `wake:true` to ALSO re-invoke a SLEEPING recipient now (deliver-and-wake) — targeted to exactly the addressees, never a broadcast. Returns the assigned msg_id.

guidance.when: Sharing context with another agent — "I just finished X, the next step is Y", or asking a question, or handing off a piece of work. Use wake:true ONLY when the recipient is idle/asleep and must act now (a Queen placing work onto a sleeping bee); a running recipient already sees the inject mid-turn, so wake is wasted on it.
guidance.notWhen: For an in-conversation reply to the human, just speak. For locking a file, use locks:acquire — coord:send is async/eventual, not a lock. Don't set wake:true for routine/ambient notes — a wake is a billable turn (unify-watch D-002: inject is the default, wake is the deliberate opt-in).

tools.name: coord:thread
tools.description: Reconstruct a coord thread rooted at `root_msg_id` — every entry connected via the `related_msg_id` chain, sorted by ts ascending.

guidance.when: You want the full conversation around a coord message (replies, acks, resolutions).
guidance.notWhen: For a fresh inbox sweep — use coord:inbox.

tools.name: coord:thread-post
tools.description: Post a message to a coordination thread by conversation_id (e.g. a spawned voter casting its structured ```vote``` block, or the advocate posting its ```advocate``` objection).

guidance.when: You were spawned into a vote/deliberation with a CONVERSATION_ID and need to cast your structured vote or objection into that thread.
guidance.notWhen: Replying in an open conversation you joined — use conversations:post. A direct message to an agent — coord:send.

tools.name: coord:vote
tools.description: Run a diverse-lens, confidence-weighted vote on a decision and get back a resolution (decisive) or a curated escalation (split). One voter per lens + an advocate arguing against the lead.

guidance.when: You face a genuinely uncertain, consequential choice between named options and want a diverse, anti-correlated read before committing — instead of deciding alone or escalating raw.
guidance.notWhen: A trivial or reversible choice — just decide. A pure factual lookup — use search/docs. To ask the human directly, use coord:ask-owner / coord:escalate.

tools.name: coord:watermark
tools.description: Read your coordination watermark — the last-read ISO timestamps for messages / escalations / plan-events plus the subscription notify msg_ids already surfaced. Pass `messages_since_ts` to coord:inbox to see only what is new since your last turn.

guidance.when: Turn start — the OMP coordination extension calls this to scope the inbox to new entries.
guidance.notWhen: Routine reads — coord:inbox without a watermark returns the full inbox.

tools.name: coord:watermark-set
tools.description: Advance your coordination watermark. Call at TURN END with the newest ISO timestamp you have seen on each surface. Partial update — omitted fields keep their current value. `subscriptions_fired` is replaced wholesale when supplied.

guidance.when: Turn end — the OMP coordination extension records how far you read this turn.
guidance.notWhen: Mid-turn — advancing early would hide notifications that arrive before the turn finishes.

tools.name: coord:whoami
tools.description: Return the coordination identity the server resolved for you: ownerId (the stable per-agent id), ownerLabel, source, workspaceId, userId, and your inbox_wake_key (the key a coord:send {wake:true} fires + the one coord:await-inbox watches). A debug aid for confirming how the coordination layer sees this agent.

guidance.when: Debugging identity — "what ownerId am I?" before relying on lock or message behaviour.
guidance.notWhen: Routine work — identity is resolved automatically by every coord:* and locks:* call.

tools.name: cross_harness:docs_get
tools.description: Fetch documentation pages from any registered harness by explicit slug. Batch up to 10; pass `heading` (single-slug only) for a section slice. Per-slug error envelope.

guidance.when: You have slugs from cross_harness:docs_outline and need the page contents from a specific harness (named by harnessSlug arg).
guidance.notWhen: You are inside a harness — use docs:get, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:docs_outline { harnessSlug } → cross_harness:docs_get { harnessSlug, slugs } → optionally re-fetch with { harnessSlug, slugs: [picked], heading } for surgical reads.

tools.name: cross_harness:docs_outline
tools.description: Outline of any registered harness's documentation by explicit slug. For engineers operating outside a harness context who need to query a specific harness's docs. Per-run cached.

guidance.when: You are not inside a harness context (no spawn URL harness slug) but need a specific harness's documentation. Pass harnessSlug explicitly.
guidance.notWhen: You are already inside a harness (ctx.harnessSlug is set) — use docs:outline instead, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:docs_outline { harnessSlug } → cross_harness:docs_get { harnessSlug, slugs }.

tools.name: cross_harness:docs_search
tools.description: Keyword search across any registered harness's documentation by explicit slug. Returns ranked hits (slug, title, description, excerpt). For out-of-harness engineers who need to find content in a specific harness without scanning its outline by hand.

guidance.when: You have specific terminology in mind and want to find which page in a specific harness covers it. Faster than scanning cross_harness:docs_outline by hand when the section name is non-obvious.
guidance.notWhen: You are inside a harness — use docs:search, which auto-targets your harness. You do not know which harness to query — list with `harness:list` or `cross_harness:docs_outline` per slug first.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:docs_search { harnessSlug, query } → cross_harness:docs_get { harnessSlug, slugs: [top-hit] }.

tools.name: cross_harness:inbox
tools.description: Read messages addressed to a harness (status pending|all|other; optional role filter).

guidance.when: You need to see messages addressed TO a specific harness across senders. The cross-harness analog of `messages:inbox`.
guidance.notWhen: For YOUR (the calling principal's) inbox, use `messages:inbox`. For sent items, use `cross_harness:outbox`.

tools.name: cross_harness:outbox
tools.description: Read messages a harness sent (cross-schema scan by from_slug).

guidance.when: You need to see what a specific harness sent — across recipients. Cross-harness analog of `messages:outbox`.
guidance.notWhen: For YOUR outbox, use `messages:outbox`. For incoming, use `cross_harness:inbox`.

tools.name: cross_harness:plans_get
tools.description: Fetch the full parsed structure of one plan in any harness by explicit slug: frontmatter, ## Now, items with effectiveStatus, decisions. Read-only.

guidance.when: You have a slug + harness from cross_harness:plans_list (or know both directly) and need the plan contents.
guidance.notWhen: You are inside the target harness (ctx.harnessSlug is set) — use plans:get, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:plans_list → cross_harness:plans_get { harnessSlug, slug }.

tools.name: cross_harness:plans_list
tools.description: List plans of any registered harness by explicit slug. For agents operating outside a single harness context who need to query another harness's plans. Read-only — writes go through ambient plans:*.

guidance.when: You are not inside a harness context (or want to inspect a different harness from outside) and need a directory of that harness's plans. Pass harnessSlug explicitly.
guidance.notWhen: You are already in the target harness (ctx.harnessSlug is set) — use plans:list, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:plans_list { harnessSlug } → cross_harness:plans_get { harnessSlug, slug }.

tools.name: cross_harness:plans_search
tools.description: Keyword search across plans of any registered harness by explicit slug. Scopes: title, now, items, decisions, prose. Read-only.

guidance.when: You're looking for prior work in another harness and don't have a slug. Pass harnessSlug + query.
guidance.notWhen: You are inside the target harness — use plans:search, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:plans_search { harnessSlug, query } → cross_harness:plans_get { harnessSlug, slug } on the top hit.

tools.name: cross_harness:recent_activity
tools.description: Workspace-wide recent activity feed (ts, harness_slug, action, subject, actor) from harness_shared.audit_log.

guidance.when: User asks "what's been happening across all my harnesses?", "any cross-harness activity?". The workspace-level activity feed.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE harness's activity, use `harness:status`. For your own audit trail, use `audit:list`.

tools.name: cross_harness:supervisor_notes
tools.description: Read supervisor notes for a harness (id, body, source, created_at).

guidance.when: You need the supervisor's annotations on a harness — context the supervisor logged that's not in audit_log.
guidance.notWhen: For escalation flags + raw notes from the on-disk files, use `harness:escalation`. supervisor_notes is the PG-backed view.

tools.name: curation:change-feed
tools.description: The Change Feed — a derived projection over completion records (work-item completions, gym proposals, plan runs). Summaries reference the originals (rationale:feed pattern). One calm rollup per tick, drill-down on demand. Filter by harness or user-requested work.

guidance.when: You want to see recent changes across the fleet (what work finished, what proposals landed) without a replicated log. Pass userRequestedOnly to see only user-facing changes; harness to scope to one project.
guidance.notWhen: For the raw fleet signals use curation:feed. For historical audit of all changes use the underlying work-items / coord-event-log directly.

tools.name: curation:feed
tools.description: Pull the curator-operator's salience-ranked fleet signals (escalations / blockers / decisions-needed / completions / progress) — the READ projection of the salience policy for a dashboard. A pure read of the CURRENT salient state (no loop, no chat-surface, no flag); the pui Fleet 'curated' view consumes this.

guidance.when: You want the curator's view of what matters across the fleet right now — the salience-ranked signals (escalations, blockers, decisions owed, recent completions) for a dashboard or status read. Pass surfaceOnly to get just the always-surface signals; harness to scope to one project.
guidance.notWhen: For the raw tool-call firehose use activity:recent / the activity stream. To make the operator SURFACE a message into the chat, that's the curation loop (flag-gated), not this read.

tools.name: db:check_drift
tools.description: Report DB migration drift — sql/*.sql files not yet applied (per harness_shared.schema_migrations). Detection only. `missing` = added since the last operator boot; restart the operator (boot auto-applies) or use db:migrate. `extra` = applied but file gone (investigate).

guidance.when: After adding a migration, or when a runtime "missing column/relation" error suggests the live DB lags the sql/ dir.
guidance.notWhen: Applying a migration — that is the boot auto-apply (restart) or db:migrate for a one-off.
guidance.chaining: missing non-empty → restart the operator (or db:migrate the file under exclusive(db-schema)).

tools.name: db:migrate
tools.description: Apply a SQL migration file, coordinated. DRY RUN unless confirm:true. With confirm, acquires exclusive(db-schema) and drains schema-dependent work (wait:{max_drain_sec}) before running psql -f <file>, then releases. The real apply also requires PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DB_MIGRATE=1. Prefer this over a raw psql -f.

guidance.when: Applying a migration / destructive DDL that could disrupt in-flight queries. Dry-run to see holders; confirm to drain + apply.
guidance.notWhen: Read-only SQL needs no lock. Never apply migrations casually on a shared box.
guidance.chaining: db:migrate { file } (dry) → review → db:migrate { file, confirm: true }.

tools.name: db:next-migration
tools.description: Atomically reserve the next migration number for a libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/<NNN>-*.sql file. Hands out GREATEST(max-on-disk, max-reserved)+1 under a pg advisory lock so two agents racing `ls | tail` never collide. Returns the number + a suggested filename/path; write the file there and it auto-applies on the next operator restart (A1 boot-apply).

guidance.when: BEFORE creating a new SQL migration file — reserve the number first instead of `ls | tail`, so a concurrent agent cannot pick the same NNN.
guidance.notWhen: Applying a migration (that is the boot auto-apply / db:migrate) or checking drift (db:check_drift).
guidance.chaining: db:next-migration { name } → write the returned path → restart the operator (boot auto-applies) or db:migrate.

tools.name: deploy:harness
tools.description: Deploy a harness's execution plane to its configured cloud frame: provision the machine, bootstrap the runtime (own loop + own embedded-pg), join it as a federated peer. The harness must have been created with a non-local `deployment` (e.g. {target:'latitude'}). Set `deployment.desktop` (true | {displays,geometry}) for a GUI-capable frame: one Xvfb display per agent slot, agents get a leased DISPLAY. Returns {ok, frame}.

guidance.when: Moving a cloud-configured harness onto a real frame so its agents run remotely (distinct IP, own Claude sub) while state federates to the local view.
guidance.notWhen: A local harness (no cloud deployment). Tearing one down — deploy:teardown. Checking status — deploy:status.
guidance.chaining: harness:create { …, deployment:{target:"latitude", desktop:true, …} } → deploy:harness { slug } → deploy:status / deploy:teardown.

tools.name: deploy:hive
tools.description: Deploy a Hive (grouping of harnesses) to a Swarm (cloud fleet): place the Queen (local|dedicated|colocated) and deploy each member harness's execution to a frame. Per-member failures are reported, not fatal. Returns {ok, result}.

guidance.when: Running a whole group of harnesses in the cloud — full-auto laptop-optional, or just to scale out execution across frames.
guidance.notWhen: A single harness — deploy:harness. Tearing one down — deploy:teardown_hive.
guidance.chaining: deploy:hive { hiveId, members, swarm } → deploy:teardown_hive when done.

tools.name: deploy:status
tools.description: Report a harness's deployment: its `deployment` config + the live frame handle (id/host/region) if deployed. Returns {ok, deployment, frame|null}.

guidance.when: Checking where a harness runs (local vs which cloud frame) and the frame's reachable host.

tools.name: deploy:teardown
tools.description: Tear down a harness's cloud frame — DESTROY (not stop) to end billing. No-op if nothing is deployed. Returns {ok, destroyed}.

guidance.when: Done with a cloud harness (or to stop its billing). Teardown destroys the machine so it stops costing money.
guidance.notWhen: Pausing temporarily — there is no stop; destroy + redeploy is the model (frames are cattle).

tools.name: deploy:teardown_hive
tools.description: Tear down a Hive — DESTROY every member execution frame + the Queen control frame (ends all billing). Pass the same hiveId + members + queen placement used to deploy. Returns {ok, destroyed, failed}.

guidance.when: Done with a deployed Hive (or to stop all its billing). Frames are cattle — destroy + redeploy is the model.

tools.name: dev:activity
tools.description: Most-recent tool invocations across selected workspaces (live activity feed).

guidance.when: Diagnostic feed of recent workspace activity — for dashboards and debugging. Lower-detail than `audit:list`.
guidance.notWhen: For agent action audit, use `audit:list`. dev:activity is for the /dev panel, not for analysis.

tools.name: dev:audit
tools.description: Cross-workspace audit_log feed (last N hours).

guidance.when: Dev-panel audit view — filtered + paginated for UI display.
guidance.notWhen: For analysis or LLM consumption, use `audit:list` directly. dev:audit is a UI-shaped projection.

tools.name: dev:build_status
tools.description: Local-host build mtime + bin/prod log tail + dev/prod server reachability.

guidance.when: Read recent build status from the dev panel — pass/fail per harness.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE harness's smoke tests, use harness-specific tools. dev:build_status is the cross-harness dev panel feed.

tools.name: dev:coord_categorize
tools.description: Categorize the coord_event_log `messages` corpus into lifecycle buckets (completion/claim/intent/restart/ack/finding) vs the irreducible contextual residual. The instrument for coord-lifecycle-automation D-006: re-run after each phase; contextualPct + automatedPct are the headline metrics.

guidance.when: Measure coord-lifecycle automation progress — how much free-text coord is predictable lifecycle vs genuinely contextual.
guidance.notWhen: To read your inbox use coord:inbox; this is an aggregate measurement over the whole corpus, not a feed.

tools.name: dev:dogfood_substrate_status
tools.description: Hyperbee substrate diagnostic: booted harnesses, per-row health verdict, workspace summary. The substrate is always active (no flag gate). Mirrors /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-health.

guidance.when: Investigating substrate boot state, claim error rates, or workspace-level dogfood health. The substrate always boots, so run this any time after the operator has started.
guidance.notWhen: For per-harness Insights or feature-level data, use the harness:* tools. This is the dogfood substrate layer specifically.
guidance.chaining: Pair with reading the agent-insights/substrate-flag-flip-runbook page for what to do if verdicts come back degraded/unhealthy.

tools.name: dev:event_emitter
tools.description: Replay-buffer probe — emits N tick events with serial ids. Dev-only.

tools.name: dev:harnesses
tools.description: List harnesses across selected workspaces with health verdict for each.

guidance.when: Dev-panel harness enumeration with diagnostic columns (active connections, recent errors).
guidance.notWhen: For ordinary list, use `harness:list`. dev:harnesses is the diagnostic projection.

tools.name: dev:hello-card
tools.description: Phase E fixture: returns a minimal mcp-ui card so external clients can verify UI rendering. Args: { greeting? }.

tools.name: dev:ipc_echo
tools.description: IPC transport verification — echoes the message back as a small typed event stream.

tools.name: dev:omp_session
tools.description: Find and read the omp session JSONL file for a spawn_id, by cwd + start-time match against ~/.omp/agent/sessions/.

guidance.when: Inspect an OMP CLI session's state — useful when debugging long-running CLI flows.
guidance.notWhen: For PRODUCTION agent runs, the orchestrator owns sessions. dev:omp_session is the CLI-tool inspector.

tools.name: dev:pg_active_queries
tools.description: List current pg_stat_activity rows (pid, state, query, duration) for the operator database.

guidance.when: Diagnostic: list currently-running PG queries (pg_stat_activity). Use when investigating slow / hung queries.
guidance.notWhen: For routine diagnostics, the /dev/pg panel is enough. Use this tool when scripting an investigation.

tools.name: dev:pg_health
tools.description: PostgreSQL version + connection counts (total/active/idle) for the operator database.

guidance.when: Diagnostic snapshot of PG health — connections, longest query, lock count. For the /dev/pg dashboard.
guidance.notWhen: For application-level health, use `harness:health`. pg_health is the database layer.

tools.name: dev:pg_table_sizes
tools.description: List tables in a pg schema with total size, index size, and estimated row count. Defaults to harness_shared.

guidance.when: Diagnostic: per-table sizes + row counts. Use when investigating storage growth.
guidance.notWhen: For application data analysis, query the relevant tools directly. pg_table_sizes is an ops view.

tools.name: dev:processes
tools.description: Inventory of agent-related processes on this host (run.sh, omp, claude, paperclip, pty, next) with cmdline, cwd, and inferred harness/workspace.

guidance.when: List tracked processes (delegates, plugin subprocesses, orchestrator children) for the /dev panel.
guidance.notWhen: For ACTIVE spawns, use `orchestrator.list_active`. For delegates, use `delegates:list`. dev:processes is the unified diagnostic view.

tools.name: dev:rate_governor_status
tools.description: Snapshot the fleet rate-limit layer now: live config (maxSimultaneousAgents + AIMD floor), fleet cap vs in-flight vs AIMD-effective concurrency, per (provider, model-class) governor buckets (paused/until, in-flight vs maxConcurrent, RPM/ITPM/OTPM headroom), and recent usage telemetry (token throughput, $spend, usage% where a provider ceiling is known). Buckets are empty until a governed agent turn has run. Use to see whether the fleet/gym is currently rate-limit-paced, paused, or AIMD-throttled.

guidance.when: Diagnose whether agent spawns / meridian calls are being paced or paused by the rate-limit governor (e.g. "why are runs slow / stalled?"), or read the fleet cap / effective concurrency / usage% the top-bar shows.
guidance.notWhen: Service up/down — dev:service_health. Migration drift — db:check_drift. EDITING the cap — operator:rate_limit_config.

tools.name: dev:restart
tools.description: Restart the operator dev server, coordinated. DRY RUN unless confirm:true. With confirm, acquires exclusive(dev-server) and drains current users (wait:{max_drain_sec}) before restarting, then releases (broadcasts "back up"). The real restart also requires PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DEV_RESTART=1 on the host. Prefer this over a raw systemctl restart.

guidance.when: You need to restart the dev server (e.g. to pick up a lib/** edit). Run dry first to see who is using it; then confirm to drain + restart.
guidance.notWhen: Just probing the server — that needs no restart. Never restart casually on a shared box; it disrupts every agent using the app.
guidance.chaining: dev:restart (dry) → review holders → dev:restart { confirm: true, max_drain_sec } → connection drops as it restarts.

tools.name: dev:service_health
tools.description: Probe the dev services now (:3070 operator, :3055 vite, :4321 shop, :3350 scout, :3001 web, :8082 code-server, plus the Tauri desktop via its dev-bridge eval + IPC socket + recent error toasts) — up/down + status + latency. The desktop entry reports present:false when no desktop is running. Use before relying on a service or after a "connection refused".

guidance.when: Confirm which dev services are up before testing against one, or diagnose a "connection refused" / stale-server symptom.
guidance.notWhen: File/lock contention — that is locks:queue. Migration drift — db:check_drift.

tools.name: dev:session_detail
tools.description: Drilldown for one spawn_id: agent metadata, tool invocations timeline, child spawns, related chats.

guidance.when: Read full detail of one /dev session — request history, env, traces.
guidance.notWhen: For the SESSION LIST, use `dev:sessions` first.

tools.name: dev:sessions
tools.description: Cross-workspace agent sessions, one row per spawn_id with started/ended/tool_count/error_count/duration totals.

guidance.when: List recent /dev panel sessions — used by the dev UI to populate session pickers.
guidance.notWhen: For application AGENT chat sessions, use `agent_chats:list`. dev:sessions is the panel's own concept.

tools.name: dev:state_counter
tools.description: Demo state-shaped tool: ticks a counter and publishes each tick via ctx.publishState. Reconnect-resilient by construction.

tools.name: dev:telemetry
tools.description: Per-tool invocation rollup (count, error rate, p50/p95) across selected workspaces over the last N hours.

guidance.when: Read recent telemetry datapoints (errors, slow requests). For the /dev/telemetry dashboard.
guidance.notWhen: For per-agent audit, use `audit:list`. telemetry is observability-shaped, not action-shaped.

tools.name: discovery:hives
tools.description: Browse the P2P hive directory — the verified hives this peer has seen announced on the well-known directory topic (title · description · owner · member harnesses). Best-effort gossip: joining a listed hive still runs the full admission/attestation flow. Feeds the pui apiary-pane + the desktop HiveDirectoryPanel.

guidance.when: You want to see hives available to join across the P2P network (the browse list behind the apiary pane / HiveDirectoryPanel).
guidance.notWhen: To list the workspace-local deployed hive frames (hiveControlFrames) use the harness/hive surfaces. To actually join a listed hive, run the join-shared-harness flow per member topic.

tools.name: discovery:set_hive
tools.description: Create or edit a hive's P2P directory listing — title, description, and visibility (public = announce to the global directory; invite = invite-scoped topic only; private = never announced). Saves the metadata to the workspace registry and announces it per visibility so peers can browse + join it.

guidance.when: You want to publish a hive to the P2P directory so other peers can discover + join it, or edit an existing listing (title/description/visibility).
guidance.notWhen: To deploy a hive’s execution frames use deploy:hive. To browse OTHERS’ hives use discovery:hives. Setting visibility:private withdraws a hive from the directory (it stops being re-announced; peers age it out via TTL).

tools.name: docs:get
tools.description: Fetch documentation pages by slug — your harness's docs (in a harness), your project's docs (PAPERCUSP_PROJECT_DOCS_ROOT env var), or the Papercusp framework reference (papercusp-su callers only). Batch up to 10; pass `heading` (single-slug only) for a section slice. Per-slug error envelope.

guidance.when: You have slugs from docs:outline and need page contents. Use `heading` (single-slug) when only one section of a long page is relevant.
guidance.notWhen: You do not yet know the slug — call docs:outline first. To fetch another harness's docs from outside, use cross_harness:docs_get.
guidance.chaining: docs:outline → docs:get { slugs } (batch up to 10) → optionally re-fetch with { slugs: [picked], heading } for surgical reads.

tools.name: docs:outline
tools.description: Return the documentation table-of-contents for your context — your harness's docs (in a harness), your project's docs (PAPERCUSP_PROJECT_DOCS_ROOT env var), or the Papercusp framework engineering reference (papercusp-su callers only). Cached per run. Call this FIRST when you need design context; drill in via docs:get.

guidance.when: You need design context, architectural rationale, or "how does X work" answers and have not yet called docs:outline this run.
guidance.notWhen: You already called docs:outline this run — cached. For prose recall (chats, escalations, brainstorms) use search:fulltext. To explore another harness from outside, use cross_harness:docs_outline.
guidance.chaining: docs:outline → docs:get { slugs: [...] }. Use { slug, heading } when only one section of a long page is relevant.

tools.name: docs:search
tools.description: Keyword search across your context's documentation — your harness's docs (in a harness), your project's docs (PAPERCUSP_PROJECT_DOCS_ROOT env var), or the Papercusp framework reference (papercusp-su callers only). Returns ranked hits (slug, title, description, excerpt).

guidance.when: You have specific terminology in mind (a function name, concept, or component) and want to find which doc page covers it. Faster than scanning the outline when the section name is non-obvious.
guidance.notWhen: You do not know what to search for — call docs:outline first. For PG-stored prose (chats, escalations) use search:fulltext. To search another harness from outside, use cross_harness:docs_search.
guidance.chaining: docs:search → docs:get { slugs: [top-hit] } (or { slug, heading } if the hit excerpt names a specific heading).

tools.name: events:await
tools.description: Register a one-shot WAKE subscription on an exact event key (e.g. lock:grant:<ticket>, plan-run:finished:<id>, or any key a source/peer will events:emit) — the named sugar for watch(key,{wake:true,once:true}). When it fires you are re-invoked — a live managed-pty session gets the wake injected as a turn; an exited session is resumed with the wake reason as the prompt; an open terminal we cannot inject gets an inbox nudge and is resumed when it exits. Then END YOUR TURN — do not poll or hold the connection.

guidance.when: You need X-to-happen-before-you-proceed and X is announced as an event: a lock grant, a plan-run finishing, a peer answering, CI/deploy landing, a custom key a collaborator will emit. Register, optionally tell the emitter the key, then end your turn and sleep.
guidance.notWhen: Ambient interest in an area — that is topics:subscribe (notify; never wakes). Sub-minute waits inside one turn — just do the bounded blocking call. Recurring schedules — the pot/routines own time-based wakes; an await is ONE-shot.
guidance.chaining: events:await { event } → end your turn. On wake, the turn text carries the event + payload — continue the blocked work. events:cancel to retract; events:status to inspect your active awaits + recent wakes.

tools.name: events:cancel
tools.description: Cancel one of your active events:await registrations (await_id — you will not be woken), or ACK a pending/parked wake delivery you already saw via the inbox nudge (delivery_id — you will not be resumed for it). Pass at least one.

guidance.when: The thing you were waiting on no longer matters (cancel the await), or a parked wake reached you in-turn via the inbox and you handled it (ack the delivery so the system does not also resume you).
guidance.notWhen: A fired await needs no cancel (one-shot — it already cleared). You cannot cancel or ack a peer’s.
guidance.chaining: events:status to find the await_id / delivery_id → events:cancel.

tools.name: events:emit
tools.description: Fire an event key through the await-event primitive: every agent with an events:await on the key is woken (durable delivery — pty-inject / session-resume / inbox ladder); an optional `to` list additionally receives a coord inbox notification (notify policy — never wakes). Use the key your waiter registered (events:await tells them what to wait on).

guidance.when: Announcing that the thing a peer is blocked on has happened: their requested work is done, an artifact landed, a decision resolved. Pair with events:await — the waiter registers the key, you emit it.
guidance.notWhen: General status narration — lifecycle auto-emits + work_items:complete already cover it. Conversation — coord:send. If nobody could plausibly be awaiting the key and you have no `to`, the emit reaches no one (it is not a log).
guidance.chaining: Peer: events:await { event: K } → you: do the work → events:emit { event: K, summary } → peer wakes.

tools.name: events:graph
tools.description: Inspect the event-reaction reactive graph: every registered rule as an `on → fire` edge (the Events file + emits desugar + plugin/blueprint rules), with its condition kind, mode, and source. With recent:true, also returns the reactions that actually fired (from tool_invocations) with their cause-chain — the answer to "why did this fire?".

guidance.when: You want to see the declarative "when X, fire Y" wiring — what reactions exist, what triggers them, and (recent:true) what has actually fired lately with its cause-chain. Pass `on` to see only the rules that fire on a given tool.
guidance.notWhen: To register a rule, use the events registry API in code (registerReactionRule) or a tool's `emits` field — there is no runtime "add a rule" tool by design (rules are curated code). For the live worker activity stream use `activity:recent`.

tools.name: events:status
tools.description: Inspect the await-event surface: your active awaits, your recent wake deliveries (with channel + status), and optionally the workspace wake meter (per-agent wake counts, last 24h — the wake-storm detector).

guidance.when: Checking what you are (still) waiting on, whether a wake fired and via which channel, or whether the fleet is wake-storming (meter: true).
guidance.notWhen: Reading your message stream — that is coord:inbox. Following an area — topics:feed.

tools.name: features:get
tools.description:
When to use: User names a specific feature ("the auth one", "F-AUTH-001") and you need its body / acceptance criteria.

When NOT to use: For a list of features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`. For changes over time, use `features:history`.

Chaining: Follow `harness:list_features` or `features:search` to find the id.

guidance.when: User names a specific feature ("the auth one", "F-AUTH-001") and you need its body / acceptance criteria.
guidance.notWhen: For a list of features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`. For changes over time, use `features:history`.
guidance.chaining: Follow `harness:list_features` or `features:search` to find the id.

tools.name: features:history
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what changed on feature X?", "who edited the spec?", or you need a timeline of edits.

When NOT to use: For the CURRENT body, use `features:get`. For cross-feature audit, use `audit:list`.

guidance.when: User asks "what changed on feature X?", "who edited the spec?", or you need a timeline of edits.
guidance.notWhen: For the CURRENT body, use `features:get`. For cross-feature audit, use `audit:list`.

tools.name: features:list_related
tools.description:
When to use: You have a feature and need to find related ones — tag overlap, shared chunks, dependency neighbors.

When NOT to use: For free-text "find features about X", use `features:search`. For ALL features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`.

Chaining: After `features:get`, use this to discover the neighborhood.

guidance.when: You have a feature and need to find related ones — tag overlap, shared chunks, dependency neighbors.
guidance.notWhen: For free-text "find features about X", use `features:search`. For ALL features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`.
guidance.chaining: After `features:get`, use this to discover the neighborhood.

tools.name: features:search
tools.description:
When to use: Free-text query for features matching a topic ("auth", "error handling") — use when the user names a concept, not a specific feature id.

When NOT to use: For specific feature id, use `features:get`. For ALL features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`. For cross-resource search, use `search:query`.

guidance.when: Free-text query for features matching a topic ("auth", "error handling") — use when the user names a concept, not a specific feature id.
guidance.notWhen: For specific feature id, use `features:get`. For ALL features in a harness, use `harness:list_features`. For cross-resource search, use `search:query`.

tools.name: features:tag_vocabulary
tools.description:
When to use: You need the set of known feature tags before tagging a new one — keeps tags consistent across the harness.

When NOT to use: For finding features BY a tag, use `features:search` (free-text) or `features:list_related`.

guidance.when: You need the set of known feature tags before tagging a new one — keeps tags consistent across the harness.
guidance.notWhen: For finding features BY a tag, use `features:search` (free-text) or `features:list_related`.

tools.name: flags:get
tools.description: Resolve one Papercusp feature flag to a boolean for this host.

tools.name: flags:list
tools.description: List every Papercusp feature flag with its resolved boolean state for this host. Use to discover what features are gated, audit V1 ship state, or check whether a flag is on before suggesting work that depends on it.

guidance.when: Before recommending or executing work that lives behind a feature flag (snapshots, templates, marketplace, oracle, harness phases, cloudflare publish).
guidance.notWhen: For runtime user-facing flag reads, use the /api/flags/bootstrap endpoint from the client.

tools.name: flags:set
tools.description: Flip a Papercusp feature flag on or off in PostHog. High-risk: changes app-wide behavior. Provide a clear reason; it is recorded for audit.

guidance.when: User explicitly asks to enable / disable a feature, OR Papercusp is being prepared for a release and the V1 ship state needs to be set.
guidance.notWhen: For ad-hoc testing of UI behavior, prefer the PostHog dashboard so changes are visible to other agents and humans.

tools.name: fleet:admit
tools.description: Ask the backpressure governor whether a spawn is affordable (global spend ceiling + per-harness/user bulkhead + circuit breaker + role credits). Debits the buckets/credit on admit; consumes nothing on refusal.

guidance.when: Before spawning an agent, to bound runaway fleet spend. Unconfigured scopes are unconstrained, so this is a no-op until the curator seeds governor cells via fleet:governor.
guidance.chaining: fleet:governor (seed buckets/circuits/credits) → fleet:admit (per spawn) → spawn if admitted.

tools.name: fleet:assignments
tools.description: The canonical "who's on what" query: per-agent presence + plan-item claims + work-item claims unified (claim-primary, holder liveness joined in). Each live agent carries its ordered work-list — `doing` (head-of-line), `queued` (items in rank order), `load` (work-item count) — the externalized per-bee TodoWrite the Queen reads for placement (load → warm-inject vs fresh slot; head-of-line → evict judgment; the ordered plan → affinity). Surfaces orphaned claims (live lease, dead holder = abandoned work) and declared-but-unclaimed intents.

guidance.when: Answering "who's running / what is agent X doing / what is X's ordered work-list / how loaded is X / is anyone on plan P". This is the state query AND the placement-decision read — use it instead of scanning coord:inbox or replaying lifecycle messages.
guidance.notWhen: You want to be notified of future changes (subscribe the fleet_assignment change-feed / your coord subscriptions) or you need full message history (coord:inbox).
guidance.chaining: fleet:assignments { plan } → see an orphaned claim → work_items:release / plan_items:release to free it, or coord:send the holder. fleet:assignments { agent } before messaging an agent about its work.

tools.name: fleet:bee_mail
tools.description: Read one bee's coordination mail by ownerId: its INBOX (messages addressed to it, or broadcast) and its OUTBOX (messages it sent). The observer view behind the bee-dossier dock pane — distinct from coord:inbox, which reads YOUR own inbox. Read-only; no heartbeat.

guidance.when: Rendering the bee-dossier pane, or inspecting what a specific bee has received/sent without being that bee.
guidance.notWhen: Reading YOUR own inbox (use coord:inbox — it also heartbeats your presence). Deriving fleet state / who is on what (use fleet:assignments).
guidance.chaining: fleet:selected_bee {} (poll the selection) → fleet:bee_mail { owner_id } + fleet:assignments { agent: owner_id } for the full dossier.

tools.name: fleet:cancel
tools.description: Cancel a spawn subtree: mark every active descendant cancelled and release its claims + locks NOW. The structured-concurrency abort — use it instead of waiting for leases to expire.

guidance.when: A human/operator aborts a unit of work, or a supervisor tears down a doomed subtree. Cancels the named spawn AND all its descendants transitively, freeing their locks + work-item/plan-item claims immediately.
guidance.notWhen: To cancel a single leaf with no children — that is the same call with a leaf spawn_id, but prefer it when you specifically mean the whole subtree.
guidance.chaining: fleet:tree (inspect the subtree) → fleet:cancel { spawn_id }.

tools.name: fleet:drain
tools.description: Signal a running bee to gracefully wind down (checkpoint, release locks/claims, return work-list, exit). Distinct from fleet:cancel (hard kill). The bee can cooperate or request deferral (propose/dispose). The Queen waits bounded time before reclaiming the slot. Returns immediately; the drain is async.

guidance.when: You (the Queen) want to reclaim a bee slot: the occupant has low-priority work, is blocked, or the priorities have shifted. Send a drain cue to give the bee a chance to hand off cleanly.
guidance.notWhen: The bee is actively running a high-priority task (let it finish naturally). Or if immediate slot reclaim is critical (use fleet:cancel). Or if the bee is unresponsive (use fleet:cancel after a timeout).
guidance.chaining: fleet:drain { bee_id } → (later, bounded) fleet:assignments { agent: bee_id } (check if the bee has released its slot) → fleet:spawn { role: "bee", brief: ... } (spawn fresh).

tools.name: fleet:governor
tools.description: Configure the backpressure governor: set a token bucket (spend ceiling/bulkhead), a circuit breaker, or a credit pool; grant credits; or record a spawn success/failure against a circuit.

guidance.when: Seeding or tuning fleet backpressure (the curator owns this). scope_key examples: "global", "harness:papercup", "user:alice", "role:worker".
guidance.chaining: fleet:governor { op:"set_bucket", scope_key:"global", capacity, refill_per_sec } → fleet:admit per spawn.

tools.name: fleet:selected_bee
tools.description: Get or set the ephemeral "selected bee" for the bee-dossier dock pane. With no args, RETURNS the currently selected bee (the bee pane polls this). With `select`, PUBLISHES the selection (the swarm/Fleet pane calls this when its cursor moves). In-memory, per-workspace, non-durable — a transport between the two pui dock processes, never persisted.

guidance.when: Driving the desktop chat dock's bee-dossier pane: the swarm pane sets the selection on cursor move; the bee pane reads it to know which bee to render.
guidance.notWhen: You want durable assignment state or "who is on what" — use fleet:assignments. This holds only the transient UI selection.
guidance.chaining: Fleet pane: fleet:selected_bee { select: { owner_id } } on cursor move. Bee pane: fleet:selected_bee {} (poll) → fleet:assignments { agent } + fleet:bee_mail { owner_id } for the dossier.

tools.name: fleet:spawn
tools.description: Spawn one agent of a role into a registered harness (project). Returns a spawn_id immediately; the run is tracked durably in the nursery — watch it with fleet:tree, stop it with fleet:cancel. role="worker" requires chunk.

guidance.when: The user asks to launch an agent on a piece of work — "spawn a validator in <harness>", "put a worker on <feature>", "have a scoper break down X". The spawn is fire-and-forget: acknowledge the launch and check fleet:tree later.
guidance.notWhen: For answering a question you already know — spawning is for new work, not lookups. For the durable feature pipeline, file a work_item and let the harness autoloop dispatch it.
guidance.chaining: fleet:spawn → (later) fleet:tree { spawn_id } to watch → fleet:cancel { spawn_id } to abort.

tools.name: fleet:supervise
tools.description: Report a crashed spawn. The supervisor restarts the strategy's set (one_for_one/one_for_all/rest_for_one) within the restart-intensity budget, or tears the subtree down + escalates to a human when it is crash-looping.

guidance.when: A supervised child exited abnormally and you (the control supervisor / curator) must decide restart-vs-escalate. Returns the restart set, or the escalation id when the crash-loop bound is breached.
guidance.notWhen: For a clean human abort — that is fleet:cancel, not a crash.
guidance.chaining: detect crash → fleet:supervise { spawn_id } → (restart the returned set) | (handle the escalation).

tools.name: fleet:tree
tools.description: Read a spawn subtree (the nursery): every descendant with its status, owner, role, and the work it serves, plus whether the root can complete (no live child).

guidance.when: Before fleet:cancel (see what would be torn down) or before completing a nursery (the completion gate refuses while a child lives).
guidance.chaining: fleet:tree → fleet:cancel { spawn_id }.

tools.name: generators:publish
tools.description: Publish the item-set your feature discovered (a scan/enumerate/audit result) so a completion-time generative wave (`for_each: { from_feature: <your feature> }`) can mint one child feature per item — each blocked_by your feature, so they run only after you finish. Idempotent (re-publishing replaces the set).

guidance.when: Your feature is the discovery half of a discover-then-act generative wave (the plan declares a `for_each: { from_feature: <you> }` wave) and you have produced the concrete list of items the downstream wave should fan out over.
guidance.notWhen: Your work has no downstream generative wave, or the item-set is already known at promote time (use a promote-time `items`/`glob`/`sql` resolver instead).
guidance.chaining: Call once near the end of your run, after the scan/enumeration is complete and verified.

tools.name: goals:get
tools.description:
