When to use: User names a specific goal and wants the rationale / acceptance criteria.

When NOT to use: For a list of goals, use `goals:list` first.

Chaining: Follow `goals:list` to find the id.

guidance.when: User names a specific goal and wants the rationale / acceptance criteria.
guidance.notWhen: For a list of goals, use `goals:list` first.
guidance.chaining: Follow `goals:list` to find the id.

tools.name: goals:list
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what are we trying to do?", "what are my goals?", or you need a goal id before calling `goals:get`.

When NOT to use: For TASKS (concrete TODOs), use `tasks:list`. Goals are the higher-level intent; tasks are how you get there.

Chaining: Pair with `goals:get` for the full body.

guidance.when: User asks "what are we trying to do?", "what are my goals?", or you need a goal id before calling `goals:get`.
guidance.notWhen: For TASKS (concrete TODOs), use `tasks:list`. Goals are the higher-level intent; tasks are how you get there.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `goals:get` for the full body.

tools.name: gym:judge
tools.description: Score a gym run's distilled trace with the frozen Opus judge (the only grader of record), using the target blueprint's rubric. Pass {intent, projectContext, distilledTrace, rubric?} where rubric mirrors the target's blueprint.gym.rubric (omit → GYM_JUDGE_RUBRIC_V1). Returns {d1,d2,d3,composite,rationale,judgeModel,rubricHash,costUsd,...}. Reasons ABOVE the harness's own validator (intent/spec-gaps, quality, process).

guidance.when: Scoring a completed gym run for the optimizer — the subjective reward the proposer optimizes. Use the TARGET blueprint's gym.rubric so a coding vs research target is judged on its own dimensions.
guidance.notWhen: Deterministic guardrails (regressions, planted-bug) — that is gym:signals, which the optimizer cannot game. Literal spec conformance — that is the target harness's own validator.
guidance.chaining: gym runner → collect+distill trace → gym:judge (rubric from target) → proposer reflects on the rationale.

tools.name: gym:signals
tools.description: Evaluate a target blueprint's deterministic gym signals (un-gameable guardrails) over one run's inputs. Pass `signals` (names from the target's blueprint.gym.signals) + any of {preTests, postTests, plantedBug, harnessOutputText}. Returns {results:[{name,value,applicable}], unknown, known}. Built-ins: regressionsFromTests (needs pre+post tests), plantedBugCaught (needs plantedBug+harnessOutputText).

guidance.when: Scoring a gym run's deterministic guardrails — the optimizer cannot game these, so they gate/monitor a variant independently of the judge. Resolve the TARGET blueprint's declared gym.signals by name.
guidance.notWhen: Subjective quality scoring — that is the frozen judge (gym:judge). Running the pipeline — the gym runner.
guidance.chaining: gym runner → collect run inputs (tests/output) → gym:signals → feed results into the proposer + the trace summary.

tools.name: harness:create
tools.description: Create a harness and instantiate a Blueprint into it. Provide an existing repo `path` OR `parentDir`+`folderName` to make a new dir; choose the blueprint via `blueprintId` (resolved local → installed → built-in, e.g. "coding"/"research" or a Cupboard-installed id) OR an inline `blueprint` object. The blueprint's knobs.requiresRepo decides git-init: coding → a git repo, research → a repo-less state dir. Registers the harness, provisions its PG schema, writes the git-canonical .papercusp/blueprint.yaml. Returns {ok, slug, path, blueprint}.

guidance.when: Spinning up a new managed harness (coding from a repo, or a repo-less research harness) configured by a blueprint. The agent-authorable path to a new harness.
guidance.notWhen: Running an existing harness (orchestrator). Authoring a blueprint without creating a harness — blueprint:create/extend.
guidance.chaining: blueprint:extend/validate → harness:create { slug, path|parentDir+folderName, blueprintId|blueprint }.

tools.name: harness:escalation
tools.description: Read escalation + supervisor-notes for a harness (PG-canonical; falls back to disk).

guidance.when: User asks "what's flagged?", "what got escalated to the supervisor?", or you need to see the supervisor's notes on a harness.
guidance.notWhen: For general "what's wrong with X" (open issues), use `issues:list`. Escalation files are a specific, narrower view than the issue list.

tools.name: harness:generate-from-repo
tools.description: Generate a coding harness from an EXISTING git repo (kind #1 creation). Deterministically detects the test command (and VERIFIES it by running it once), the toolchain, monorepo/frontend flags, and harvests AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/TESTING.md into an `extends: coding` blueprint override; validates it; then creates the harness via harness:create. Skips if the repo already has .papercusp/blueprint.yaml. Use `dryRun` to preview the generated override without creating. Returns {ok, slug?, skipped?, override?, detection, validation}.

guidance.when: Onboarding an existing code repository as a managed coding harness — you want the blueprint inferred from the repo (test command, stack, monorepo/frontend) rather than authored by hand.
guidance.notWhen: The repo already has a .papercusp/blueprint.yaml (it is skipped — edit the file instead). Creating a repo-less / research harness, or one whose blueprint you author explicitly — harness:create with blueprintId/blueprint. Generate-from-plan (kinds #2/#3) is out of scope.
guidance.chaining: harness:generate-from-repo { slug, path, dryRun:true } → (inspect override) → harness:generate-from-repo { slug, path } (creates). Or blueprint:validate the returned override.

tools.name: harness:get
tools.description:
When to use: User asks about a specific harness by name ("tell me about sheets", "what's the status of forms") and you need its row + feature counts.

When NOT to use: For a list of all harnesses, use `harness:list`. For LIVE health (escalated/blocked), prefer `harness:status` or `escalations:get` — `harness:get` is the static record.

Chaining: Follow `harness:list` if you don't have the slug. Follow with `harness:status` if you also need live counts.

guidance.when: User asks about a specific harness by name ("tell me about sheets", "what's the status of forms") and you need its row + feature counts.
guidance.notWhen: For a list of all harnesses, use `harness:list`. For LIVE health (escalated/blocked), prefer `harness:status` or `escalations:get` — `harness:get` is the static record.
guidance.chaining: Follow `harness:list` if you don't have the slug. Follow with `harness:status` if you also need live counts.

tools.name: harness:health
tools.description: Read consolidated health verdict for a harness (alive, escalated, feature counts, ghost rate, checks).

guidance.when: User asks "is sheets healthy?", "is the harness running?". Single fast snapshot — alive, escalated flag, feature-status counts.
guidance.notWhen: For LIVE phase + activity (recent audit events), use `harness:status`. For open issues, use `issues:list`.

tools.name: harness:list
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what harnesses do I have?", "show me my projects", or you need a slug to feed into harness:get / harness:status.

When NOT to use: For ONE specific harness, use `harness:get`. For a single harness's live health (active/done counts), use `harness:status`.

Chaining: Pair with `harness:get` (detail) or `harness:status` (live counts) once you have the slug.

guidance.when: User asks "what harnesses do I have?", "show me my projects", or you need a slug to feed into harness:get / harness:status.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE specific harness, use `harness:get`. For a single harness's live health (active/done counts), use `harness:status`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `harness:get` (detail) or `harness:status` (live counts) once you have the slug.

tools.name: harness:list_features
tools.description: List features for a harness slug (optionally for a specific phase: staging, testing, production).

guidance.when: User asks "what features does sheets have?" or you need a feature id before calling `features:get`. Pass a phase to scope (staging = upcoming, testing = in-flight, production = done).
guidance.notWhen: For ONE feature's detail, use `features:get`. For the harness as a whole, use `harness:list`/`harness:get`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `features:get` for body, `features:history` for change log.

tools.name: harness:markdown_index
tools.description: Load the per-harness markdown index (filename + headings + anchor ids) across the workspace.

guidance.when: User asks "what docs exist?", "where's the spec for X?", or you need to navigate to a specific section of the harness's markdown.
guidance.notWhen: For the CONTENT of an indexed file (state files in any one harness), use `docs:get` — context-aware: when called inside a harness it serves that harness's content. For wiki-style backlinks (`[[name]]` references), use `wiki:backlinks`. This tool's unique value is the cross-harness sweep in one call.

tools.name: harness:membership
tools.description: List / add / remove / move which workspaces a harness belongs to. Registry edits only — never touches the harness folder or its run data.

guidance.when: User asks to move a harness to another workspace, share/link a harness into a second workspace, see which workspaces a harness is in, or remove a harness from a workspace. op=list reads; op=add/remove/move mutate.
guidance.notWhen: To CREATE a brand-new harness from a folder/repo, use the harness create flow (POST /api/harness/projects), not this — membership only links/moves harnesses that already exist somewhere.

tools.name: harness:migrate-config-json
tools.description: One-time backfill (deprecate-harness-config-json-2026-06-06): lift every harness's legacy `.papercusp/config.json` INSTANCE content (phase/phases/dept + per-instance knob overrides) into the workspace-PG registry, so the file is no longer read as a config source. Idempotent — already-migrated / file-less harnesses are skipped; scaffold contract artifacts (harness_token/parent_slug/slug) are left in the file. Returns {ok, scanned, migratedCount, results:[{slug,fields}]}.

guidance.when: Once per workspace after the config.json→PG cutover, to lift any pre-existing harness config.json instance content into the registry. Safe to re-run (idempotent).
guidance.notWhen: Routine operation — this is a one-time backfill. New harnesses persist instance config to PG directly; nothing reads config.json on the live path.

tools.name: harness:pending_reviews
tools.description: List unresolved pending-review entries for a harness slug (optionally per phase).

guidance.when: User asks "anything pending review?", "what needs my approval?". The dedicated tool for plan-review state.
guidance.notWhen: For open ISSUES (problems, bugs), use `issues:list`. For all pending hook events, use `pending_events:list`.

tools.name: harness:phase_path
tools.description: Resolve the on-disk path for a (harness_slug, phase) pair. Phase = staging|testing|production.

guidance.when: You need the absolute filesystem path for a harness phase before reading files inside it.
guidance.notWhen: For listing files INSIDE the phase dir, use `harness:markdown_index` or `harness:list_features`. This tool only resolves the dir path.

tools.name: harness:plan_reviews
tools.description: Load all harness plan-review entries (slug, verdict, summary, mtimeMs) across the workspace.

guidance.when: Cross-harness plan-review status — "what plans have been reviewed", "any verdicts?". Single-harness lookups use `harness:pending_reviews`.
guidance.notWhen: For one harness's pending reviews, use `harness:pending_reviews`. For all-harness LIVE health, use `harness:list` then `harness:status` per slug.

tools.name: harness:status
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what is harness X doing right now?", "is sheets active?", or you need recent-activity counts + phase.

When NOT to use: For "what's WRONG with X", use `issues:list` (problems-side view). For static facts about the harness, use `harness:get`.

guidance.when: User asks "what is harness X doing right now?", "is sheets active?", or you need recent-activity counts + phase.
guidance.notWhen: For "what's WRONG with X", use `issues:list` (problems-side view). For static facts about the harness, use `harness:get`.

tools.name: harness_docs:anchor
tools.description: Anchor a manual doc to the code it documents (its subject_ref) so drift is tracked; optionally verify it against HEAD. Unanchored manual docs remain allowed but flagged "not drift-tracked".

guidance.when: A human-authored doc should be drift-tracked: declare what code it covers. Run after writing/editing the doc, or to fix a wrong anchor.
guidance.notWhen: For a generated doc use harness_docs:record (it sets a generated baseline). To only re-confirm currency use harness_docs:verify.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:anchor { documents } → (later, on a drift nudge) harness_docs:verify.

tools.name: harness_docs:ingest
tools.description: Backfill a harness's existing FS docs into the typed drift-tracked model: anchor docs that declare/imply a subject as manual records (baselined to HEAD). One-time per harness; idempotent.

guidance.when: After this harness has existing docs/*.md that predate the typed model, to make the ones with a declared/inferable subject drift-tracked.
guidance.notWhen: Record-less docs already show as "not drift-tracked" via the merged read — ingest is only needed to anchor docs that declare a subject. No need to run repeatedly.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:ingest → harness_docs:list (review which anchored) → harness_docs:anchor (fix any wrong/missing anchors).

tools.name: harness_docs:list
tools.description: List a harness's merged docs (generated · manual · augmented) with source badges + drift status (fresh/stale/review/untracked), and the active doc's body + augmented overlay. Supersedes the FS-only project-docs read.

guidance.when: You want a harness's project docs WITH provenance + freshness — which are generated vs human, which are stale, which are not drift-tracked.
guidance.notWhen: For Papercusp framework docs use docs:get/outline. For raw markdown without metadata the old project-docs endpoint still exists but is superseded.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list → harness_docs:regenerate (stale generated) / harness_docs:verify (stale manual) / harness_docs:set_overlay (add human nuance).

tools.name: harness_docs:record
tools.description: Record a generated doc's provenance + drift anchor (subject_ref) and stamp it generated-from the harness repo's current HEAD. Call this once per generated doc immediately after writing the file, passing what you read.

guidance.when: You (the documenter) just wrote or refreshed a generated doc file (docs/features/F-<id>.md, a guide). Call once per doc with the feature + the exact files/symbols you read.
guidance.notWhen: For a human-authored manual doc, use harness_docs:anchor instead (it sets a verify baseline, not a generated baseline). Do not call for docs you only read.
guidance.chaining: Write the .md file → harness_docs:record { docId, documents }. The freshness sweep then tracks it against future commits.

tools.name: harness_docs:regenerate
tools.description: Request a documenter regeneration of a stale generated/augmented doc. Enqueues it (preserving any human overlay); the doc refreshes when the documenter re-records it.

guidance.when: A generated doc is stale (its subject code changed) and you want it refreshed.
guidance.notWhen: For a manual doc use harness_docs:verify. To preserve human nuance across the regen, add it via harness_docs:set_overlay first.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list (find stale generated) → harness_docs:regenerate.

tools.name: harness_docs:set_overlay
tools.description: Attach a human "augmented" overlay to a doc — nuance that rides on top of the generated body and survives regeneration. Empty string clears it.

guidance.when: A generated doc is accurate but missing the human "why"/caveats you want preserved across regenerations. Add it as an overlay rather than hand-editing the generated body (which a regen would lose).
guidance.notWhen: To change the generated body itself, fix the code/feature and regenerate. For a fully human doc, author it as a manual doc.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list → harness_docs:set_overlay { overlay }.

tools.name: harness_docs:verify
tools.description: Re-verify a manual doc: stamp its drift baseline to the current HEAD and mark it fresh. Use after reviewing a doc the freshness sweep flagged for re-verify.

guidance.when: A manual doc was flagged for re-verify (its subject code changed) and you confirmed it's still accurate — or you just edited it to match.
guidance.notWhen: For a generated doc use harness_docs:regenerate. To set the anchor in the first place use harness_docs:anchor.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list (find review docs) → read → harness_docs:verify.

tools.name: hive:create
tools.description: Stand up a NEW local hive (root-only): provision a home harness running the pot (kind:'hive') blueprint, stamp it harness_kind:'hive', and optionally wake the Queen. Composes the harness-provision primitives + pot:wake, transactional with rollback. NOT callable from a bee/parented agent — hives are peers, never nested. Cloud placement is a separate step (deploy:hive).

guidance.when: Standing up a NEW local hive (its home harness + Queen) in one call. Operator/user only.
guidance.notWhen: Deploying an EXISTING hive to a cloud frame — deploy:hive. A plain non-hive harness — harness:create. From a bee — not allowed (spin a kind:harness subharness instead).
guidance.chaining: hive:get { slug } to inspect; pot:declare-wake to set the cadence; deploy:hive to place it on a Swarm; hive:dissolve to tear it down.

tools.name: hive:dissolve
tools.description: Tear down a local hive (root-only, destructive — pass confirm:true): clear the Queen's wake so she won't re-wake, cancel every live bee + its subtree, and deregister the home harness. Optionally drop the harness PG schema (default keep). Idempotent. Does NOT destroy a deployed cloud frame — that is deploy:teardown_hive.

guidance.when: Permanently tearing down a local hive — stop the Queen, cancel its bees, deregister it. Operator/user only.
guidance.notWhen: Destroying a deployed cloud frame (the Queen/member execution planes) — deploy:teardown_hive. Pausing a hive without tearing down — pot:declare-wake { mode:none }. From a bee — not allowed.
guidance.chaining: hive:get { slug } to inspect before; deploy:teardown_hive first if the hive is deployed to a Swarm.

tools.name: hive:get
tools.description: The full state of one hive: its home harness + deployment + wake schedule (scheduled?, next/last fire, event subscriptions), its live bees with {doing, queued, load}, and its todo-work frontier depth. Composes resolveHive + fleet:assignments + work_items — the one call for "how is hive X doing".

guidance.when: You want one hive in depth: is the Queen scheduled to wake, who are the bees and how loaded, how much work is queued.
guidance.notWhen: A list of all hives — hive:list. The raw per-agent fleet view across the workspace — fleet:assignments.
guidance.chaining: hive:list to find the slug; pot:wake to fire the Queen now; pot:declare-wake to change the cadence; hive:dissolve to tear it down.

tools.name: hive:list
tools.description: The workspace-local hives (kind:'hive' harnesses — the Pots): each with its home slug, deployment target, wake (scheduled? next/last fire), and a live-agent count. The local-lifecycle view; for joinable network hives use discovery:hives, for per-bee placement detail use fleet:assignments, for one hive in depth use hive:get.

guidance.when: You want the workspace-local hives (the Pots) and their wake/load at a glance.
guidance.notWhen: Browsing joinable hives across the P2P network — that is discovery:hives. The raw per-agent fleet view — fleet:assignments. One hive in depth — hive:get.
guidance.chaining: hive:get { slug } to drill into one; hive:create to add one; hive:dissolve to tear one down.

tools.name: hive:update
tools.description: Edit a hive's config: its deployment target (execution plane) and per-instance config overrides (maxCostUsd, parallelWorkers, …). A thin registry writer — no agent-lifecycle effects (never wakes/cancels). Cannot change harness_kind (a hive cannot reclassify). Root-only.

guidance.when: Changing a hive's deployment target or its per-instance config overrides (budget/parallelism knobs).
guidance.notWhen: Waking/pausing the Queen — pot:wake / pot:declare-wake. Placing/removing bees — fleet:*. Deploying to a cloud frame — deploy:hive.
guidance.chaining: hive:get { slug } to see the current config; deploy:hive to act on a changed deployment target.

tools.name: hooks:known
tools.description: Static well-known hook-event allowlist (kernel set; plugin-registered hooks extend this).

guidance.when: Static enum of supported hook event names — use to validate an event string before firing or registering for it.
guidance.notWhen: For PENDING events queued up, use `pending_events:list`. For firing an event, use `plugins:fire_event`.

tools.name: improvements:capture
tools.description: Capture a papercusp improvement you discovered (a friction, a missing affordance, a bug in the tooling) as a durable, claimable, `papercusp-improvement`-tagged work-unit. kind=bug → auto-implement-eligible later; change|feature → human-reviewed. Search-first: declines an obvious duplicate (link to it instead) unless force. Pass `paths` when you know the files involved — it feeds the protected-path safety gate.

guidance.when: You hit a papercusp DX / tooling / code friction worth fixing but out of your current scope. File it here so it lands in the triage backlog instead of being lost. Use kind=bug for something broken, kind=change for a desired improvement, kind=feature for net-new (the last two stay human-gated). Include `paths` (repo-relative files involved) when known — the auto-implement risk gate reads them.
guidance.notWhen: A problem in a MANAGED harness/project (not papercusp itself) — that is issues:create with that harness scope. Something needing real design — write a plan (plans:new) and capture with kind=feature linking it. A passing question — coord:ask.
guidance.chaining: improvements:capture { kind, title, paths? } → (later) improvements:digest triages it → an agent claims + fixes it self/inline, or the auto-implement loop picks up the bugs and improvements:resolve closes them.

tools.name: improvements:digest
tools.description: Triage the captured papercusp-improvement backlog: scores + dedups every improvement work-unit and splits it into the auto-eligible lane (kind=bug, no protected surface) vs the human-review queue. Read-only — surfaces the queue, implements nothing. (P-010) Supports per-Hive scope filtering.

guidance.when: To review the papercusp self-improvement backlog — what is captured, what is auto-eligible vs needs a human, and which items look like duplicates to merge. The human-facing triage view. (P-010) Pass harnessSlug to filter to a specific Hive's ideas.
guidance.notWhen: You want one improvement in full — issues:get { id }. You want to file one — improvements:capture. You want to browse another area — topics:feed { topic }.
guidance.chaining: improvements:digest → issues:get / issues:claim on a queued item → fix it self/inline (or improvements:capture to add more).

tools.name: improvements:resolve
tools.description: Close the loop on a captured papercusp improvement you worked: outcome `fixed` (requires testsRun — the verification evidence) marks it resolved so it leaves the queue; `could-not-fix` releases it for a retry (exhausted retries route to a human); `needs-human` routes it to the human queue permanently.

guidance.when: You finished working a dispatched/claimed improvement (usually as the implement worker). Fixed + tests green → outcome fixed with the evidence. Could not make it work → could-not-fix with what you tried. The fix would touch a protected surface (operator-core safety / deploy machinery / a migration) or needs judgment → needs-human.
guidance.notWhen: You only want to comment progress — issues:comment. You are closing a non-improvement issue — issues:close. The item was never captured (no EI/WI id) — improvements:capture it first if it is worth tracking.
guidance.chaining: improvements:digest → (dispatch/claim) → implement + test → improvements:resolve { id, outcome, summary, testsRun }.

tools.name: improvements:triage
tools.description: Queen-turn triage: read the scored improvements:digest and type-route each idea (product→place, process→gate/gym). Updates idea lifecycle state with the Queen's decision. (P-010) Supports per-Hive scope filtering. (P-012) Routes product-ideas to target project, process/prompt-ideas to papercusp gate.

guidance.when: To triage captured ideas: read the digest summary, classify each by type, decide (place/gate/gym/reject), and record the Queen's judgment. (P-010) Pass harnessSlug to triage a specific Hive's ideas. (P-012) Type-routing: product→place as work-item in target; process/prompt→papercusp gate/gym.
guidance.notWhen: You want to READ ideas — use improvements:digest. You want to CAPTURE — use improvements:capture. You want implementation status — use improvements:resolve.
guidance.chaining: improvements:triage → work_items:create/update for placed ideas, or coord:escalate for human-gate ideas.

tools.name: inbox:triage
tools.description: Triage one attention item (the operator inbox PASS): downgrade a false positive or resolve it → the auditable "Handled by operator" tier; escalate an under-flagged item or confirm a real one → the Decisions tier. Record WHY in `note` (required on downgrade/resolve). The downgrade is always visible + auditable, never a silent vanish.

guidance.when: Operator inbox PASS — run FIRST each wake over the Decisions tier: re-tier an attention item after reading it (downgrade noise, escalate something a worker under-flagged, confirm/resolve a real decision), always recording the why in `note`. Leave the inbox clean before sleeping.
guidance.notWhen: Acting on the item itself (resolve an escalation → coord:resolve; mark a plan item done → plans:set-status). Messaging the owning agent → coord:message-agent.

tools.name: intel:artifacts
tools.description:
When to use: You need the Intel-panel-shaped view of recent artifacts — grouped + summarized for UI display.

When NOT to use: For loading a specific artifact body, use `artifacts:load`. For listing artifacts a tool produced, use the tool's response. intel:artifacts is the panel feed.

guidance.when: You need the Intel-panel-shaped view of recent artifacts — grouped + summarized for UI display.
guidance.notWhen: For loading a specific artifact body, use `artifacts:load`. For listing artifacts a tool produced, use the tool's response. intel:artifacts is the panel feed.

tools.name: intel:spawn_tree
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what triggered this?", "show me the lineage of agent X", or you need the parent-child spawn graph for an Intel-panel-style view.

When NOT to use: For LIVE running spawns only, use `orchestrator.list_active`. spawn_tree is historical + structural; list_active is the now-snapshot.

guidance.when: User asks "what triggered this?", "show me the lineage of agent X", or you need the parent-child spawn graph for an Intel-panel-style view.
guidance.notWhen: For LIVE running spawns only, use `orchestrator.list_active`. spawn_tree is historical + structural; list_active is the now-snapshot.

tools.name: issues:claim
tools.description: Claim an issue (assign it to yourself) before you start fixing it, so others know it is owned. Auto-subscribes you. Pass assignee to claim on behalf of another agent.

guidance.when: You are about to start work on an issue — claim it first so two agents do not duplicate the fix.
guidance.notWhen: Just reading/triaging (no claim needed). To drop a claim, issues:release.
guidance.chaining: issues:list → issues:claim → (fix) → issues:close / issues:promote.

tools.name: issues:close
tools.description: Set an issue's lifecycle state: resolved (fixed/answered), closed (won't-fix / no longer relevant), or open (reopen). Resolving notifies all subscribers, including mention-mode.

guidance.when: An issue is fixed (resolved) or is being dropped without a fix (closed). Reopen with state=open if it recurs.
guidance.notWhen: Promoting it to a tracked fix feature — issues:promote (which keeps it open/fixing until the feature lands).

tools.name: issues:comment
tools.description: Add a note to an issue's comment thread. Subscribers are notified. Use for investigation findings, repro details, or a status update on an issue you are working.

guidance.when: You have something to add to an existing issue — a repro, a root-cause finding, a decision, or progress.
guidance.notWhen: Editing the issue itself (issues:update) or resolving it (issues:close).

tools.name: issues:create
tools.description: File an engineer/SU issue — a real problem you discovered but are not fixing right now. Tag topics so agents subscribed to that area see it. Returns the issue id (EI-<n>). Dup-check with issues:search first.

guidance.when: You hit a real problem mid-work that is out of your current scope (or that you are deferring) and want it tracked + visible to others in the area. Tag the relevant topics.
guidance.notWhen: A passing question with no clear owner — use coord:ask (knowledge-first). Something you are fixing right now in-scope — just fix it. A validator finding inside a pipeline run — that goes through the validator pipeline, not here.
guidance.chaining: issues:search (dedup) → issues:create { topics } → issues:claim when you start → issues:close on resolution; issues:promote to mint a fix feature.

tools.name: issues:get
tools.description: Read one engineer issue in full — fields, topic tags, the comment thread, and its links (e.g. what it blocks).

guidance.when: You have an issue id (from issues:list/search) and want its detail before claiming, commenting, or fixing.
guidance.notWhen: Scanning many — use issues:list.
guidance.chaining: issues:list → issues:get → issues:claim / issues:comment / issues:close.

tools.name: issues:link
tools.description: Link an issue to another object — e.g. this issue blocks a plan item or a feature. rel = blocks | relates | duplicates | fixes. target = a {kind, ref} like {plan_item, '<plan-slug>#P-003'} or {feature, '<harness>#F-012'} (a feature ref MUST be harness-qualified — bare 'F-012' is rejected). Pass unlink:true to remove.

guidance.when: An issue blocks specific work (a plan item / feature) — link it so that work is shown blocked until the issue closes; or relate/dedup two issues. A feature ref is harness-qualified: "<harness>#<feature_id>" (e.g. "papercup#F-12").
guidance.notWhen: Tagging it to a topic area — issues:tag.

tools.name: issues:list
tools.description: List engineer/SU issues. Filters: state (open|resolved|closed), scope, assignee, severity, topic (issues tagged it), mine (assigned to you). The agent-facing problem tracker — distinct from the validator pipeline (harness:status shows that).

guidance.when: To see open problems in an area before starting work, find something to pick up, or check what you are assigned. Filter by a topic to see everything filed against that area.
guidance.notWhen: You want validator-pipeline findings for one harness — that is harness:status. You want one issue in full — issues:get.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → issues:list { topic } → issues:get → issues:claim.

tools.name: issues:promote
tools.description: Promote an issue into an F-FIX feature so the harness pipeline fixes it. A harness-scoped issue mints into its harness; an operator-scope issue needs a target harness. Records the linked feature; the issue stays open until the fix lands.

guidance.when: An issue is a real defect that should be FIXED by the pipeline (not just tracked or answered) — promote it to mint + link the fix feature.
guidance.notWhen: A question/discussion (resolve it), a nit you would not spend a feature on, or an issue already linked to a feature.
guidance.chaining: issues:get → issues:promote { harness } → the F-FIX feature dispatches in that harness; issues:close when it lands.

tools.name: issues:release
tools.description: Release (unassign) an issue so someone else can pick it up — e.g. you are blocked, deprioritizing, or handing off.

guidance.when: You claimed an issue but are not going to finish it — release so it is pickable again.
guidance.notWhen: You finished it — issues:close instead.

tools.name: issues:search
tools.description: Full-text search engineer issues by title/body. Use before issues:create to avoid filing a duplicate, or to find a known problem.

guidance.when: Before filing an issue (dedup), or to locate an existing one by keywords.
guidance.notWhen: You want a filtered list by state/topic/assignee — issues:list.
guidance.chaining: issues:search → issues:get / issues:comment (add to the existing one instead of a dup).

tools.name: issues:subscribe
tools.description: Follow a specific issue so its comments/updates/resolution inject into your inbox. mode = full | digest | mention. Pass unsubscribe:true to stop. (To follow an area, use topics:subscribe.)

guidance.when: You care about one specific issue (you reported it, depend on it, or can contribute) and want its updates pushed to you.
guidance.notWhen: You want everything in an area — topics:subscribe is the scalable unit.

tools.name: issues:tag
tools.description: Add or remove topic tags on an issue. Tagging it with a topic routes it to everyone subscribed to that topic — the main way an issue reaches the right people. topics:list to see/create topics.

guidance.when: An issue belongs to a relevance area (e.g. zero-cache, federation) so the people following that area should see it.
guidance.notWhen: The topic does not exist yet — topics:create it first (prefer an existing one).
guidance.chaining: topics:list → issues:tag { add:[topic] }.

tools.name: issues:update
tools.description: Edit an issue's title / body / severity / kind / found-during / linked feature. Notifies subscribers. (State → issues:close; tags → issues:tag; comments → issues:comment.)

guidance.when: Refine an issue you or someone else filed — clarify the title/body, re-rate severity, correct a mislabeled kind (bug↔change — the kind picks the auto-implement lane, so keep it honest), or attach the feature that will fix it.
guidance.notWhen: Resolving it (issues:close), adding a note (issues:comment), or routing it to a topic (issues:tag).

tools.name: lexicon:active_pack
tools.description: The active brand pack's full term→label map (every term key → singular/plural forms) plus the pack id. Resolved via the server-side lexicon twin so the `papercusp-the-hive` flag is respected. The single source of truth for any non-React/non-server surface (e.g. the Rust pui) that needs the live lexicon without duplicating the packs.

guidance.when: A client outside the React/server lexicon wiring (the pui TUI, a CLI) needs the active term labels; fetch once at startup and re-fetch on a flag change if a push rail exists.
guidance.notWhen: You are in React (use the useLexicon hook) or server code (import term() from the lexicon module) — those resolve in-process.

tools.name: locks:acquire
tools.description: Claim a set of files for exclusive editing. Returns ok+lock_id on success, or busy+contention details on failure. On contention prefer wake_on_grant:true — queue a waiter ticket + a one-shot wake subscription and return immediately; you END YOUR TURN and are re-invoked when the cascade grants you the locks (no polling, no held turn). wait={max_sec:N} (≤300) is the legacy blocking wait for short same-turn needs. Paths MUST be repo-relative POSIX (no leading ./, no //, no trailing /, no .., no backslashes, no absolute paths) — the server canonicalizes equivalent spellings to one lock key but rejects malformed ones; resolve symlinks caller-side before claiming.

guidance.when: For a DELIBERATE multi-file claim you hold across several edits AND the commit — acquire once for the whole set, release after committing. Per-edit locking is already automatic on every client (the PreToolUse/tool_call hook acquires + releases around each individual Edit/Write/apply_patch), so the gap this fills is the edit→commit window the hook cannot cover.
guidance.notWhen: Read-only inspection needs no claim. A single incidental edit needs no manual call — the hook covers it. Do NOT wrap every edit in acquire/release; that duplicates the hook and churns the lock.
guidance.chaining: On ok: make your edits → commit → locks:release { lock_id }. On busy: wake_on_grant:true → end your turn; the wake turn carries your lock_id + TTL (already running) — edit, then release. Only block (wait) when you need the lock within THIS turn and the holder is about to finish; events:cancel + locks:cancel_wait to retract a queued wake.

tools.name: locks:acquire_granular
tools.description: Acquire a multi-granularity intention lock on a path NODE (a file, a directory/subtree, or the harness root ""). mode "X" = own the subtree exclusively (a directory lock for a refactor, or a file write); "S" = read the whole subtree; "SIX" = read the subtree while writing one node; IS/IX are the intention modes (usually derived for you). The lock places the matching intention on every ancestor incl. the harness root, so a harness-exclusive (X on "") now conflicts with any descendant file lock. All-or-nothing — you get the whole lock-set or a conflict list. Release with locks:release_granular.

guidance.when: A directory/subtree refactor (mode X on the dir), reading a whole subtree (S), or coordinating file-vs-harness-level work the per-edit lock is too fine for. Use "" as the path to take/contend the harness root.
guidance.notWhen: A single-file edit — the per-edit hook + locks:acquire already cover that. Cross-resource coordination (dev-server / db-schema) — use locks:acquire_resource.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_granular { path, mode:"X" } → on ok do the work → locks:release_granular { lock_id }. On conflict, inspect the returned conflicts and pivot/retry.

tools.name: locks:acquire_resource
tools.description: Acquire a NAMED resource (must be registered; see locks:list). mode:"shared" = "I am using it" (many coexist); mode:"exclusive" = "I need to restart/mutate it" (granted only once shared holders drain to zero). For exclusive, set wait:{max_drain_sec:N} (≤300) to block while existing shared holders finish — new shared acquisitions are refused meanwhile. Release with locks:release_resource.

guidance.when: Before relying on a shared resource (mode shared), or before a destructive action on it like restarting the dev server (mode exclusive). Registered resources only — check locks:list.
guidance.notWhen: File edits — use locks:acquire (the per-edit hook already covers those). An unregistered ad-hoc name — register it first (locks are useless if names diverge).
guidance.chaining: shared: acquire_resource{mode:shared} → use it → release_resource. exclusive restart: acquire_resource{mode:exclusive,wait:{max_drain_sec}} → on ok+held do the restart → release_resource (signals it is back up).

tools.name: locks:cancel_wait
tools.description: Abandon a queued waiter ticket. Returns cancelled=true if the wait was active; cancelled=false means a grant raced (you now hold a lock you didn't want — call locks:release immediately).

guidance.when: Mid-wait, when the user redirects you to other work or you decide a different approach.
guidance.notWhen: After you've already received an ok response from locks:acquire — there's no waiter to cancel.
guidance.chaining: On cancelled=false → locks:release { all_mine: true } to free the lock you got handed.

tools.name: locks:check_command
tools.description: Check a raw shell command against the named-lock registry: does it touch a resource with an exclusive (restart/migration) in flight? Returns decision (allow | warn | block) + the matched resources. The verdict a raw-Bash gate consumes.

guidance.when: A hook (or you) wants to know if a destructive command would collide with an in-flight exclusive hold before running it.
guidance.notWhen: Acquiring a lock — use locks:acquire_resource. File edits — locks:queue.
guidance.chaining: block → wait / coordinate; warn → proceed with care; allow → run.

tools.name: locks:heartbeat
tools.description: Extend a held lock's TTL. Returns extended=true on success; extended=false means the lock had already expired or been stolen.

guidance.when: For edits expected to take >15 min, call once at the halfway mark.
guidance.notWhen: For short edits — the default 20-min TTL covers it. Heartbeating every minute is wasteful.

tools.name: locks:heartbeat_resource
tools.description: Extend a named-resource lease you hold (by lock_id) for another ttl_sec. Owner-checked; no-op if the lease already lapsed.

guidance.when: Holding a named resource longer than its TTL — heartbeat near the halfway mark.
guidance.notWhen: Short holds within one TTL window. Released locks need no heartbeat.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_resource → (long work, heartbeat periodically) → locks:release_resource.

tools.name: locks:list
tools.description: List registered named resources (name, rule, enforcement level) and who currently holds each, with a draining flag. The authoritative discovery surface for resource locks — only registered names are acquirable.

guidance.when: Before acquiring a named resource (to learn the exact name + the rule), or to see who holds a resource / whether it is draining.
guidance.notWhen: File-lock contention — that is locks:queue.
guidance.chaining: locks:list → locks:acquire_resource { resource, mode }.

tools.name: locks:queue
tools.description: Read the active locks and pending waiters for a workspace. Optionally filter by paths (overlap) or owner. Pass include_completed=true to also return terminal waiters from the last 24h (diagnostics).

guidance.when: Diagnostics — "what are the other agents doing?" or "why am I blocked?". Cheap, MVCC read.
guidance.notWhen: Before every acquire — locks:acquire already returns busy context. Use queue when the user asks.

tools.name: locks:release
tools.description: Release a held lock set. Pass lock_id (with optional paths filter) for a specific lock, or all_mine=true to release every lock owned by this agent. Fires the grant cascade for waiting agents.

guidance.when: Immediately after the edit is committed. On context loss / restart, call with all_mine=true to release everything.
guidance.notWhen: Mid-edit. The lock should outlive the edit by enough that no other agent races between release and PR merge.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire → edit → locks:release { lock_id }. Or: session-end → locks:release { all_mine: true }.

tools.name: locks:release_granular
tools.description: Release a granular intention lock-set you hold, by lock_id. Frees the leaf node + all of its ancestor intention locks in one call. Owner-checked.

guidance.when: As soon as the subtree/directory work the lock guarded is done.
guidance.notWhen: While still working under the lock. Release is owner-checked — you can only drop your own lock-set.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_granular → work → locks:release_granular { lock_id }.

tools.name: locks:release_resource
tools.description: Release a named-resource lock you hold — pass lock_id (preferred) or the resource name. Releasing the last shared holder completes a pending exclusive's drain; releasing an exclusive frees the resource.

guidance.when: As soon as you are done using a shared resource, or immediately after an exclusive action (e.g. the dev-server restart) completes.
guidance.notWhen: While still using the resource. Do not release another agent's lock — release is owner-checked and only drops your own rows.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_resource → use/act → locks:release_resource { lock_id }.

tools.name: memory:forget
tools.description: Delete a specific memory entry by id.

guidance.when: When the user explicitly says "forget X" / "don't remember that anymore" / "that's wrong, drop it". Always inform the user out loud ("Removed that from memory").
guidance.notWhen: To CORRECT a memory (replace its content), use memory:update — preserves history. Only use forget for outright removal.

tools.name: memory:list
tools.description: List all memories for the current user. Supports filtering by kind and harness scope.

guidance.when: When the user asks to inspect their memory ("what have you stored about me?") or you need a filter-only query.
guidance.notWhen: For semantic lookup ("what did I say about X?"), use memory:search instead.

tools.name: memory:remember
tools.description: Store a STABLE fact about the user into persistent memory. Use one of 4 kinds (identity / preference / project / correction). For transient state, use coord — not memory.

guidance.when: When the user says "remember X" / "don't forget Y" / "next time…" / "from now on…", OR when YOU notice an error you made that would recur without persistence. ALWAYS inform the user out loud ("I'll remember that"). For project-specific facts, pass harness_slug — the fact then surfaces for anyone working in that harness.
guidance.notWhen: Default scope is per-user. Do not pass harness_slug for personal preferences. For IN-FLIGHT / ephemeral state (what you are doing right now), use coord (coord:declare-intent / coord:send) — it is delta-delivered, not a semantic store.
guidance.chaining: After writing, the persona prompt will surface this entry on the next turn's pre-turn injection. No need to call memory:search to verify.

tools.name: memory:search
tools.description: Search the user's persistent memories by semantic similarity. Returns matched facts ranked by relevance.

guidance.when: When the user references specific context from past sessions ("what did I tell you about pricing?"). Pre-turn auto-injection covers most cases; only call this for targeted lookups.
guidance.notWhen: For lookups by exact metadata (kind), use memory:list — it's faster than vector search for filter-only queries.
guidance.chaining: Pair with memory:update / memory:forget when the user corrects something you recall.

tools.name: memory:update
tools.description: Replace the content of a memory entry while preserving its id and metadata.

guidance.when: When the user corrects something you previously stored ("actually it's Daniel, not Dan"). Find the entry id via memory:search or memory:list first, then call this with the corrected content. Inform the user ("Updating my memory: …").
guidance.notWhen: To REMOVE a memory entirely, use memory:forget. To add a NEW memory without replacing one, use memory:remember.

tools.name: messages:dismiss
tools.description:
When to use: Soft-hide a message you've handled — "ignore that note", "dismiss the comment on X". Reversible (status→archived, not deleted).

When NOT to use: For deleting a message, this isn't it — dismiss is reversible. For archiving a CHAT (multi-turn), use `agent_chats:archive`.

guidance.when: Soft-hide a message you've handled — "ignore that note", "dismiss the comment on X". Reversible (status→archived, not deleted).
guidance.notWhen: For deleting a message, this isn't it — dismiss is reversible. For archiving a CHAT (multi-turn), use `agent_chats:archive`.

tools.name: messages:inbox
tools.description:
When to use: What's pending for me? Harness-level messages (directives, worker replies) — or pass `feature_id` for one feature's thread.

When NOT to use: For sent items use `messages:outbox`. To soft-hide a handled message use `messages:dismiss`.

guidance.when: What's pending for me? Harness-level messages (directives, worker replies) — or pass `feature_id` for one feature's thread.
guidance.notWhen: For sent items use `messages:outbox`. To soft-hide a handled message use `messages:dismiss`.

tools.name: messages:outbox
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what did I send?", "did the message go through?", or you need to confirm a recent send.

When NOT to use: For incoming, use `messages:inbox`.

guidance.when: User asks "what did I send?", "did the message go through?", or you need to confirm a recent send.
guidance.notWhen: For incoming, use `messages:inbox`.

tools.name: messages:send
tools.description:
When to use: Forward a note/directive to another agent. Harness-level: operator → "tell the worker to retry". Feature-scoped: pass `to_feature_id` (+ `from_feature_id`) to post on one feature's pipeline thread. Always paraphrase + confirm out loud first; sends are durable.

When NOT to use: For dispatching WORK use a `<spawn>` tag — messages are notes, spawns are work. For replying in the user's chat, just speak. To read replies use `messages:inbox` (feature-scoped via `feature_id`).

Chaining: Read replies with `messages:inbox`; soft-hide a handled message with `messages:dismiss`.

guidance.when: Forward a note/directive to another agent. Harness-level: operator → "tell the worker to retry". Feature-scoped: pass `to_feature_id` (+ `from_feature_id`) to post on one feature's pipeline thread. Always paraphrase + confirm out loud first; sends are durable.
guidance.notWhen: For dispatching WORK use a `<spawn>` tag — messages are notes, spawns are work. For replying in the user's chat, just speak. To read replies use `messages:inbox` (feature-scoped via `feature_id`).
guidance.chaining: Read replies with `messages:inbox`; soft-hide a handled message with `messages:dismiss`.

tools.name: new_subagent:approve
tools.description: BRAIN-ONLY: approve or deny a pending new_subagent spawn request. Resolves it + wakes the requester (which spawns on approve). Enforced at the dispatch layer — only the brain (operator principal) or a superuser may call it.

guidance.when: You are the brain and a new_subagent:request is pending; you have judged whether the spawn is worth it given open work + the live spawn headroom.
guidance.notWhen: You are a pipeline/worker agent — you cannot approve spawns (the gate denies you). To ASK for a spawn, use new_subagent:request.

tools.name: new_subagent:request
tools.description: Request the brain spin up a new sub-agent. Routes a typed, brain-only-approvable request; you then events:await the grant and spawn on approval. The BRAIN decides whether it is worth it (informed by the live spawn headroom + open work) — this is judgment, not a rules budget.

guidance.when: You want to spawn a sub-agent (a helper/specialist) as an autonomous initiative beyond your own role — a spawn worth a brain decision.
guidance.notWhen: You ARE the brain/operator (you allocate directly) OR this is already-decided pipeline work (the pipeline admits its own role progression) OR a human-initiated psu session (no request needed).
guidance.chaining: new_subagent:request → events:await { event: <await_event> } (end your turn) → on wake, if choice="approve", fleet:spawn { role, harness, feature }.

tools.name: notifications:recent
tools.description: List recent toast notifications shown in the app (errors, warnings, info, success).

guidance.when: Read recent toast notifications shown to the user — for "did I miss anything?" / replay.
guidance.notWhen: For PERSISTENT inbox items, use `messages:inbox`. Notifications are ephemeral toasts.

tools.name: omp:config
tools.description: Read or update the local omp CLI config tree (get / set { key, value } / unset { key }).

guidance.when: Read or set an OMP CLI config key (model, paths, env tweaks). Used during installation / first-run flows.
guidance.notWhen: For OPERATOR runtime preferences (voice, scanner), use `operator:preferences`. omp:config is the CLI tool's config.

tools.name: omp:sessions
tools.description: List, search, read, and summarize local OMP session JSONL files.

guidance.when: Search or inspect local OMP session history. Use this when a successor agent needs context from an earlier compacted/handed-off session, when debugging what an overnight OMP agent did, or when answering "what happened in that session?"
guidance.notWhen: For Papercusp harness runs stored in Postgres, use the harness/agent_chats/plans tools first. omp:sessions is specifically the local OMP JSONL transcript archive on this workstation.
guidance.chaining: Use op='list' to find a session id, op='search' to locate decisions or errors, then op='state' for compact structured state or op='get' for bounded raw entries.

tools.name: operator:audit
tools.description: Log a single operator-card lifecycle event (accepted / ignored / dispatched / dismissed / …) so the dashboard reconstruction sees it.

guidance.when: Operator-scoped audit feed — every operator action (scans fired, cards dispatched, mode flips).
guidance.notWhen: For workspace-wide audit including non-operator actors, use `audit:list`. operator:audit is the narrower operator-only stream.

tools.name: operator:budget
tools.description: Read or set the daily operator budget cap. Get is any role; set is operator only.

guidance.when: Read operator daily-spend status — todaySpendUsd, capUsd, exceeded flag.
guidance.notWhen: For voice-specific spend, use `operator:voice_spend_summary`. For raising the cap, use /settings/operator.

tools.name: operator:conv_voice
tools.description: Read or set the EL Conv AI agent voice (voice_id, optional model_id). Adds public voices to library if needed.

guidance.when: Read voice-conversation state (mode, engine, transcript). Diagnostic for the voice-converse pipeline.
guidance.notWhen: For voice PREFS (defaults), use `operator:voice_prefs`. conv_voice is runtime, not config.

tools.name: operator:converse
tools.description: Operator brain conversation turn. Self-contained: builds the prompt (role+memory+history+trigger), gates on budget, runs the LLM with agentmcp tools, records spend, post-turn mem0.add, dispatches <spawn> tags. Streams deltas + tool_calls.

tools.name: operator:credentials_status
tools.description: Masked credential status for voice providers (set/not-set + tail). Read-only — never returns raw keys.

guidance.when: Check which API credentials (EL, OpenAI, etc.) are configured + valid. Used in onboarding + diagnostics.
guidance.notWhen: For SETTING credentials, use the /settings UI directly — agents shouldn't paste secrets.

tools.name: operator:decisions
tools.description: Read recent operator_decisions rows for the active workspace (id, ts, actor, action, target, details).

guidance.when: Read the operator decision log — what flips, dispatches, and autoaccepts happened and why.
guidance.notWhen: For action audit (user-action style), use `actions:recent` or `operator:audit`. decisions is the operator-policy view.

tools.name: operator:dedup_check
tools.description: Check if a candidate title fuzzy-matches any card in `existing` above the threshold. Returns { match, threshold }.

guidance.when: Check whether a suggestion / scan candidate duplicates a recent one before committing it to the panel.
guidance.notWhen: For listing existing scans, use `operator:scans_list`.

tools.name: operator:delegate
tools.description: Delegate-to-claude streaming chat. Records the task as a work_item (kind=task), resolves session, builds MCP config, spawns claude with session resume + MCP tools; emits session→deltas→tool_calls→done. Thin sugar over work_items: writes the turn as a work_item thread comment (→ subscribe→inject to the operator) + a generated title.

tools.name: operator:multi_workspace
tools.description: Aggregation of every other workspace's last-scan snapshot (active workspace omitted).

guidance.when: List workspaces the operator can switch between — used by the workspace switcher.
guidance.notWhen: For the CURRENT workspace's harnesses, use `harness:list`. multi_workspace is the workspace enumerator.

tools.name: operator:notes
tools.description: Read or append feature-scoped operator notes (Steer primitive). { op: read|append, slug?, featureId, content?, author? }.

guidance.when: Read or update the operator's free-form note buffer — long-running scratch the user adds via /settings.
guidance.notWhen: For HINDSIGHT (cross-agent memory), use `hindsight:recall`. Notes is operator-only, user-editable.

tools.name: operator:nudge
tools.description: Arbitrate a spoken nudge — returns { fired } indicating whether the per-kind dedup window allows speaking now.

guidance.when: Send a one-shot toast to the user — "checkpoint?", "smoke failed", etc. Use sparingly; chat is the primary channel.
guidance.notWhen: For conversation, just speak in your reply. nudge is for non-conversational status only.

tools.name: operator:paused
tools.description: Read the operator pause sentinel — true when scans are suppressed.

guidance.when: Read/set the global operator-pause flag — silences scans + scanner-triggered cards across the workspace.
guidance.notWhen: For per-harness autoloop pause, use `autoloop:control`. paused is operator-global; autoloop is harness-scoped.

tools.name: operator:preferences
tools.description: List / append / remove operator preference entries (provenance-tagged markdown).

guidance.when: Read or update operator-level preferences (scan cadence, autoAccept tier, persona name, etc.).
guidance.notWhen: For VOICE prefs specifically, use `operator:voice_prefs`. For workspace-level config, use `multi_workspace`/`papercusp:list_workspaces`.

tools.name: operator:preview_prompt
tools.description: Build the operator scanner prompt for a request without running it. Useful for debug + plugin-author validation.

guidance.when: Render the operator's assembled prompt for a given trigger — debug tool to verify what the model sees.
guidance.notWhen: Production code shouldn't depend on this; it's diagnostic only.

tools.name: operator:rate_limit_config
tools.description: Read or edit the live fleet rate-limit config: maxSimultaneousAgents (fleet-wide concurrent-agent cap, honored live by the governor + dispatcher) and concurrencyFloor (the AIMD floor). Edits persist + propagate with zero restart.

guidance.when: The user wants to throttle or open up the fleet ("drop to 2 agents while I use Claude", "back to 16"), or you need the persisted cap/floor values.
guidance.notWhen: READ the live pacing/pause/usage state — dev:rate_governor_status (this tool reads the persisted CONFIG, not the live bucket state).
guidance.chaining: After a set, dev:rate_governor_status shows the new cap take effect (fleet.cap / fleet.effective).

tools.name: operator:standing_approval_mark_shown
tools.description: Mark a standing-approval candidate as first-shown (timestamp gate for voice-approve eligibility).

guidance.when: Mark a standing-approval banner as shown so it doesn't re-flash. Internal UI bookkeeping.
guidance.notWhen: For listing approvals, use `operator:standing_approvals_list`. For deciding, `operator:standing_approvals_decide`.

tools.name: operator:standing_approvals_decide
tools.description: Approve or dismiss a standing-approval candidate. Approve writes a [STANDING-APPROVE] entry to operator preferences.

guidance.when: User answered yes/no to a standing-approval prompt — record the decision so the autoaccept rule applies / doesn't.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE-OFF dispatch confirmation, just call `panel_dispatch_card` after the user yes/nos verbally. standing_approvals_decide is for the persistent rule.

tools.name: operator:standing_approvals_list
tools.description: Standing-approval candidates: capability/target pairs the operator has silently dispatched ≥3× in 24h, eligible for "always allow".

guidance.when: List standing approvals — pre-authorized actions the user said "go ahead" to once.
guidance.notWhen: For one-off pending reviews, use `harness:pending_reviews`. Standing approvals are session-persistent autoaccepts.

tools.name: operator:stats
tools.description: 7-day operator KPIs: card counts, auto-dispatch rate, dismissal rate, escalation rate, median ack latency, spend.

guidance.when: Aggregate operator stats — scans/day, dispatches/day, mode-flip counts. For dashboards / status reports.
guidance.notWhen: For LIVE state, use the specific dedicated tool. stats is historical aggregates.

tools.name: operator:trigger_state
tools.description: Read the workspace trigger-state fingerprint + raw state (used by background scanner to decide rescans).

guidance.when: Read scanner trigger state — when the next scan fires, what's pending.
guidance.notWhen: For LIVE scan results, use `operator:last_scan` or `operator:scans_list`.

tools.name: operator:voice_debug
tools.description: Read, append, or clear the process-local voice-debug ring buffer (same buffer as the agent-mcp/voice-debug route).

guidance.when: Debug snapshot of the voice engine state — engine in use, last connection, transcript queue. Diagnostic only.
guidance.notWhen: For voice preferences, use `operator:voice_prefs`. voice_debug is read-only diagnostic.

tools.name: operator:voice_prefs
tools.description: Read or partial-update operator voice prefs (engine selectors, feature toggles, agent ids).

guidance.when: Read/set voice preferences — engine, wake word, autostart, persona name.
guidance.notWhen: For runtime state of an active session, use `operator:conv_voice`. voice_prefs is user-set config.

tools.name: operator:voice_spend_summary
tools.description: Voice spend snapshot — el (Conv AI minutes), stt (today USD + caps), tts (per-K-char rate + caps), or all merged.

guidance.when: Read aggregated voice-engine spend (EL minutes, OpenAI tokens) for budget visibility.
guidance.notWhen: For operator daily budget across all surfaces, use `operator:budget`. voice_spend_summary is the voice slice.

tools.name: operator:voice_utterance_log
tools.description: Append a voice-utterance audit row (source/mode/length/persona-flags/modifications).

guidance.when: Read recent voice transcripts — what STT heard, what TTS spoke. Useful for "what did I just say?" / debugging mishears.
guidance.notWhen: For TEXT chat history, that lives in operator_turns. voice_utterance_log is voice-only.

tools.name: oracle:chat
tools.description: Single-turn Oracle assistant chat. Streams delta/tool_call/cost events; returns final assistant text.

tools.name: papercusp:list_workspaces
tools.description:
When to use: Discovery helper for superuser shells — list all workspaces in the installation. Used when scope-switching.

When NOT to use: For the CURRENT workspace details, use the operator-state APIs. papercusp:list_workspaces is the cross-workspace enumerator.

guidance.when: Discovery helper for superuser shells — list all workspaces in the installation. Used when scope-switching.
guidance.notWhen: For the CURRENT workspace details, use the operator-state APIs. papercusp:list_workspaces is the cross-workspace enumerator.

tools.name: pending_events:list
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what's queued up?", "what events are pending?", or you need to inspect the hook-event backlog.

When NOT to use: For approvals (plan reviews, escalations awaiting user yes/no), use `pending_reviews_list`. Pending EVENTS are hook plumbing; pending REVIEWS are user-facing decisions.

guidance.when: User asks "what's queued up?", "what events are pending?", or you need to inspect the hook-event backlog.
guidance.notWhen: For approvals (plan reviews, escalations awaiting user yes/no), use `pending_reviews_list`. Pending EVENTS are hook plumbing; pending REVIEWS are user-facing decisions.

tools.name: plan_items:adopt_name
tools.description: Adopt a stable agent-NAME for this session (e.g. "builder-1"). Assignment targets a NAME, not a session, so after adopting you can read your assigned items (plan_items:my_items) and claim them across interruptions. Idempotent; re-adopting overwrites this session's name.

guidance.when: At the start of a session that should act as a named agent — e.g. you were told "you are builder-1, go to your items". Adopt the name, then plan_items:my_items.
guidance.notWhen: Ad-hoc one-off work you are not coordinating by name — you can still claim unassigned pool items without a name.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:adopt_name { name } → plan_items:my_items → plan_items:claim.

tools.name: plan_items:assign
tools.description: Push-assign a plan item (P-NNN) to a stable agent-NAME. Durable intent — survives interruption; the named agent reads it via plan_items:my_items and claims it. Intra-user only: you may assign to a name you own (a fresh name is claimed for you); a name owned by another user is refused (cross-user is pull-only).

guidance.when: You are dividing your own plan work across your named agents — "builder-1 takes P-001..P-003".
guidance.notWhen: You want to start working on an item right now — that is plan_items:claim (the live grip). Handing work to another USER's agents — they pull it (you cannot push onto their machine).
guidance.chaining: plan_items:assign { harness, plan, item, assignee } → the named agent: plan_items:my_items → plan_items:claim.

tools.name: plan_items:claim
tools.description: Take the live, heartbeat-leased grip on a plan item — what you call when you actually START it. Refused if the item is assigned to a different agent-name, or unassigned in a plan whose work-group you have not joined. Returns the claim (with claim_id + lease expiry); keep it alive with plan_items:heartbeat, drop it with plan_items:release.

guidance.when: You are about to begin work on an item (yours via assignment, or pulled from the pool).
guidance.notWhen: You only want to mark intent for later without starting — that is assignment, not a claim. Renewing an existing claim — that is plan_items:heartbeat.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:claim { harness, plan, item } → work → plan_items:heartbeat (per turn) → plan_items:release when done.

tools.name: plan_items:convert
tools.description: Convert-at-pickup (D-015): pick up a plan item by converting it to a work_item in one call — takes the policy-checked plan-item lease, mints (or idempotently resumes) the work_item with you as assignee, links it back (`implements` edge + payload stamp), and auto-flips the plan item to wip. The work_item is then your execution record: work_items:complete on it reflects the plan item to done.

guidance.when: You are picking up a plan item to work it — this replaces a bare plan_items:claim: every worked item gets a tracked work_item (no untracked self-item).
guidance.notWhen: You only want the lease without an execution record (rare; plan_items:claim). The item is already converted and you hold it — just keep working; re-converting is a harmless resume.
guidance.chaining: plans:items { actionable:true } → plan_items:convert { plan, item } → work → work_items:complete { id, completion } (reflects the plan item to done) or work_items:release (returns it to todo).

tools.name: plan_items:heartbeat
tools.description: Renew your claim's lease. Send kind="activity" when you complete a unit of work (the turn-based pulse a SHARED harness needs), kind="extend" with a larger ttl_sec for a legitimately long single operation, or kind="keepalive" to prove liveness on a LOCAL harness. claim_id optional (resolved from your current claim).

guidance.when: Periodically while holding a claim — ideally once per completed turn (kind="activity"), or kind="extend" before a long uninterrupted op.
guidance.notWhen: You are done — that is plan_items:release. The claim has already lapsed — re-acquire with plan_items:claim (a lapsed claim cannot be heartbeated back to life).
guidance.chaining: plan_items:claim → plan_items:heartbeat { kind: "activity" } per turn → plan_items:release.

tools.name: plan_items:join_group
tools.description: Join a shared plan's work-group so your sessions may CLAIM unassigned items from its pool (cross-user pull-only — nobody push-assigns onto your machine). A plan with no work-group is open; declaring one gates pool pulls to members.

guidance.when: You want to help on a shared plan owned by another user — join, then pull unassigned items.
guidance.notWhen: It is your own plan / single-user — pool pulls are already open.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:join_group { harness, plan } → plan_items:status → plan_items:claim an unassigned item.

tools.name: plan_items:leave_group
tools.description: Leave a plan's work-group (stop being eligible to pull its unassigned items).

guidance.when: You are done helping on a shared plan.
guidance.notWhen: You still hold claims there — release them first (plan_items:release).
guidance.chaining: plan_items:leave_group { harness, plan }.

tools.name: plan_items:my_items
tools.description: List the plan items assigned to your agent-NAME (across all plans), each with its live claim state (active / assigned-idle). "Go to your items" resolves here. Adopt a name first (plan_items:adopt_name) or pass agent_name explicitly.

guidance.when: You were told to work on your assigned items — read them here, then claim the next idle one.
guidance.notWhen: You want unassigned pool items — those are not "yours"; see plan_items:status for the pool.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:adopt_name → plan_items:my_items → plan_items:claim { the next assigned-idle item }.

tools.name: plan_items:release
tools.description: Drop your live claim on a plan item so it returns to your assignee status (if assigned) or the pool (if pulled). Does NOT clear the assignment — the item stays yours by name; you just stop holding it. claim_id is optional (resolved from your current claim).

guidance.when: You finished (or are pausing) work on an item you claimed and want to free the live grip.
guidance.notWhen: You want to give up the item entirely — also plan_items:unassign it.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:claim → … → plan_items:release { harness, plan, item }.

tools.name: plan_items:status
tools.description: The merged per-item view of a plan: each item's disposition (pooled / assigned-idle / active / claimed-pooled / claimed-mismatch) combining the durable assignment with the live claim, plus any work-group members. The coherent answer to "who is doing what on this plan".

guidance.when: Deciding what to pick up, or auditing who holds what on a plan.
guidance.notWhen: You only want YOUR assigned items — plan_items:my_items is narrower.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:status { harness, plan } → claim a "pooled"/"assigned-idle"(yours) item.

tools.name: plan_items:unassign
tools.description: Release a plan item's assignment so it returns to the unassigned pool. The item's history persists (soft-release). Does NOT drop a live claim — release that with plan_items:release.

guidance.when: An assignment is no longer wanted — reassigning to nobody, or freeing an item back to the pool.
guidance.notWhen: You just want to stop actively working but keep the item assigned to you — that is plan_items:release (drops the live claim, keeps the assignment).
guidance.chaining: plan_items:status to see assignments → plan_items:unassign { harness, plan, item }.

tools.name: plans:add-decision
tools.description: Append a new decision to a plan. Allocates the next D-NNN id inside a lock (concurrent calls produce non-colliding ids). Auto-bumps frontmatter updated:.

guidance.when: A decision-shaped output: trade-off resolved, scope ratified, choice made between options. Capture so a fresh agent doesn't relitigate.
guidance.notWhen: Adding work units — use plans:add-item. Flipping status — plans:set-status. Updating overall state — plans:set-now.
guidance.chaining: plans:add-decision → optionally plans:set-now referencing the new D-NNN in **State:**.

tools.name: plans:add-item
tools.description: Append a new item to a phase. Allocates the next P-NNN id inside a lock. Creates the phase section if it doesn't exist. Auto-bumps frontmatter updated:.

guidance.when: New work surfaces — a chunk to do, a verification step, a follow-up. Pick the right phase (or name a new one).
guidance.notWhen: Updating an existing item — that's a direct edit, not an assisted write (the format is stable). Or status flip — plans:set-status.
guidance.chaining: plans:add-item → plans:set-status to flip newly added items off `todo` when work starts.

tools.name: plans:apply-plan-block
tools.description: Parse and apply a ```promote:plan fenced block: creates a new draft plan via plans:new → plans:set-now → plans:add-item × N → plans:add-decision × N.

guidance.when: The architect (or any agent) emitted a ```promote:plan block and the human accepted it. Pass the raw block content (everything between the fences, excluding the fence lines themselves).
guidance.notWhen: The plan already exists — use plans:set-content or the individual write verbs instead.
guidance.chaining: Returns { ok, slug }. Follow with plans:get to read the created plan.

tools.name: plans:attention
tools.description: The Planning tab's unified attention feed: plan items + coord escalations + coord messages-to-human + smoke-fails + plan-reviews + operator <report> turns, mapped to a single AttentionItem shape, grouped by plan (+ per-harness Alerts bucket), importance-sorted. Each source best-effort.

guidance.when: You want everything awaiting the human / pickable, in one importance-sorted feed — the Planning tab inbox, or to find the single most-urgent open thing.
guidance.notWhen: You only need plan items (use plans:items), or the full structure of one plan (plans:get). For the orchestrator DONE-gate use plans:items { needsHuman: true }.
guidance.chaining: plans:attention → act on an item via its kind (plans:set-status for plan items, coord:resolve for escalations).

tools.name: plans:backfill-revisions
tools.description: One-time, idempotent migration: seed the plan_revisions spine from git history — one synthetic revision per past commit (commit subject as a weak rationale, session_kind git_backfill, no session). A plan that already has revisions is skipped, so re-running is safe.

guidance.when: Once, after the revision spine ships, to give existing plans a history before their first live write — or to seed a single plan whose spine was never populated.
guidance.notWhen: Routine use. The spine is maintained automatically by every plans:* write verb; this is a migration, not an everyday tool.
guidance.chaining: plans:backfill-revisions → plans:revisions to confirm the chain.

tools.name: plans:edit
tools.description: Edit a plan in place by exact string replace (old_string → new_string), like the file Edit tool — the surgical way to fix a citation, a line, or a paragraph without resending the whole document. old_string must match exactly once (or pass replace_all). Rejects: string_not_found, string_not_unique, a result that would degrade the plan to legacy, or a lint failure. Records a plan revision. expectedHash is optional — the exact match is the concurrency guard.

guidance.when: Correcting or rewriting a SPECIFIC part of a plan body the structured verbs cannot reach — a stale citation, a wrong line, a paragraph in `## Background` or a decision body. The default for small/targeted prose fixes.
guidance.notWhen: Replacing the whole Now block (set-now), appending a decision/item (add-decision / add-item), or flipping status (set-status) — use the structured verb. A wholesale rewrite of most of the document — use plans:set-content / set-content-chunk.
guidance.chaining: Read the current text (plans:get) → plans:edit { slug, old_string, new_string }. For several edits, call plans:edit repeatedly (each is CAS-safe on its own match).

tools.name: plans:export
tools.description: Produce a plan's canonical markdown on demand (plans are PG-canonical; markdown is rendered, not stored as tracked files). `{ slug }` returns one plan's markdown; `{ toDir }` re-materializes every plan as .md files under that directory.

guidance.when: You need the raw markdown of a plan to pipe/share, or want a one-off offline dump of all plans as files.
guidance.notWhen: You want the parsed structure (items/decisions/now) — use plans:get. You want to edit a plan — use the plans:set-* verbs (they write PG).
guidance.chaining: plans:list → plans:export { slug } for the markdown of any plan.

tools.name: plans:get
tools.description: Fetch the full parsed structure of one plan by slug: frontmatter, ## Now (state + next), items with effectiveStatus, decisions. Resolves archived plans too.

guidance.when: You have a slug from plans:list and need the plan contents.
guidance.notWhen: You don't know the slug — call plans:list first. Item-only queries across plans should use plans:items.
guidance.chaining: plans:list → plans:get { slug } → optionally plans:items for cross-plan picks.

tools.name: plans:items
tools.description: Cross-plan item query. actionable=true returns pickable items (effectiveStatus="todo"). needsHuman=true returns the human's inbox. status filters by effectiveStatus. Legacy plans excluded.

guidance.when: You want to find items by status across all plans — "what can I pick up", "what needs the human", or filter one plan's items.
guidance.notWhen: You want the full plan structure (Now block, decisions, prose) — use plans:get.
guidance.chaining: plans:items { actionable: true } → plans:get { slug } for context on the picked item.

tools.name: plans:launch
tools.description: Launch an autonomous agent on a plan. Assembles the plan context bundle (plan doc + revision rationale), starts a resumable run, streams the agent, records it in plan_runs. Returns the run id + session id.

guidance.when: You want an agent to autonomously advance a plan — pick up its next actionable item and work it.
guidance.notWhen: You only want to read a plan (plans:get) or edit it yourself (the plans:set-* verbs). Resuming an existing run is a continue call, not a fresh launch.
guidance.chaining: plans:list / plans:get → plans:launch { slug } → the run streams; plans:runs lists past launches.

tools.name: plans:lint
tools.description: Validate plan files. Legacy plans are exempt. Returns errors + warnings per plan. CI should fail on any error; warnings are informational.

guidance.when: You're editing a plan and want to verify it parses cleanly, or you're running the doc-tree health check.
guidance.notWhen: You just want to read plans — use plans:list/get.
guidance.chaining: plans:lint → plans:get { slug } for the failing plan to see context.

tools.name: plans:list
tools.description: List SU plans under apps/operator/docs/plans/. One row per plan with title, status, item counts by effectiveStatus, and the ## Now next-action line. Legacy plans (no frontmatter) surface as status="draft" (flagged via isLegacy).

guidance.when: You need a directory of plans — "what plans exist", "what plans are active", or the entry point before plans:get.
guidance.notWhen: You already know the plan slug and want full contents — call plans:get directly.
guidance.chaining: plans:list → plans:get { slug } (full plan) or plans:items { actionable: true } (pickable items across plans).

tools.name: plans:new
tools.description: Create a new SU plan from the canonical template. Slug uniqueness enforced inside a lock; rejects if a file with the same slug already exists.

guidance.when: You are starting a new plan and want a templated file with valid frontmatter ready to fill in.
guidance.notWhen: You want to edit an existing plan — use plans:set-status / set-now / add-decision / add-item.
guidance.chaining: plans:new → plans:set-now (replace placeholder Now) → plans:add-item to populate Phase 1.

tools.name: plans:pause
