tools.description: Suspend orchestrator feature-picking for a plan. In-flight worker turns finish; no new features are picked until plans:start is called again. Returns { notStarted: true } if the plan was never started (op_status is null).

guidance.when: User pauses work on a plan from the UI, or an agent needs to suspend a plan without marking it done.
guidance.notWhen: The plan is done — use plans:set-run-status for run lifecycle. To mark the whole plan complete, update the frontmatter status to shipped.
guidance.chaining: plans:list to find the slug, then plans:pause { slug }. Resume with plans:start.

tools.name: plans:promote
tools.description: Promote a `plans:*` plan into a harness. Preview computes the per-feature covers mapping and lists assertions that would be extracted. Apply POSTs features to /features/import (server allocates F-AUTO-*), stores inline VAL-* assertions to harness_plan_assertions, and marks the plan's from_items as done. A wave declaring `spawn_child` is routed into a NEWLY-SPAWNED child harness instead (scaffold → auto-synthesized seed plan → import → start; preview reports the would-be child). Always emits a `plan_event` of kind=promoted.

guidance.when: A plan is ready to enter the harness — you and the human have settled the feature list and acceptance criteria.
guidance.notWhen: Routine plan edits — plans:set-now / plans:add-item already cover those. Mid-debate — promote only once the design is settled. ANTI-OVER-SPAWN (D-001, promote-spawn-child-harness): a `spawn_child` wave is justified ONLY when the work crosses a repo/worktree boundary or needs its own lifecycle/done-definition — same-repo sub-work stays as plain features in the current harness (the dispatcher already runs feature pipelines concurrently; a child harness buys no extra parallelism, only overhead). When in doubt, do NOT spawn.
guidance.chaining: spawn_child waves: re-run with apply:false first — the preview lists the child slug, seed plan, and feature count with zero side effects. A partially-failed spawn (see `spawned_children[].warnings`) is retried by simply re-promoting (idempotent: scaffold/seed/import/start all upsert or no-op).

tools.name: plans:resume
tools.description: Continue an existing plan-agent run. Sends a follow-up message into a run started by plans:launch, re-seeding the agent with the current plan and appending new turns to its transcript.

guidance.when: You want to continue a plan run — send a follow-up instruction to an agent already launched on a plan.
guidance.notWhen: Starting a fresh agent on a plan is plans:launch. Only reading a run’s past turns needs no agent at all.
guidance.chaining: plans:runs → plans:resume { runId, message } → the run streams further turns.

tools.name: plans:revision-diff
tools.description: Unified diff between a plan revision and its immediate predecessor — sourced from the plan_revisions snapshot pair, not git. Returns a `react-diff-view`-parseable patch string. Seq 1 returns the file-against-empty creation diff.

guidance.when: You have a revisionId from plans:revisions and want the patch — what exactly changed in that revision.
guidance.notWhen: You want a coarse git patch — that is plans:diff. The revision chain — plans:revisions. The current plan body — plans:get.
guidance.chaining: plans:revisions → plans:revision-diff { revisionId } for any revision.

tools.name: plans:revision-transcript
tools.description: The conversation behind a plan revision — scoped: paginated by cursor, narrowable by query, never a whole-transcript dump. Returns turns from the plan-run transcript; revisions from a direct editor save or a git backfill report available:false.

guidance.when: You need the reasoning behind a specific revision — the raw conversation, drilled into around a decision via query/cursor.
guidance.notWhen: You want the revision list with rationales — plans:revisions. You want the plan body — plans:get. Never pull a whole transcript unscoped.
guidance.chaining: plans:revisions → plans:revision-transcript { revisionId, query } → page with cursor.

tools.name: plans:revisions
tools.description: The revision chain for a plan, newest-first — one row per recorded plans:* write: seq, author (agent|human), the rationale, the session that produced it, a +/- diff-stat vs the prior revision, and timestamp. The conversation-linked counterpart to plans:history (git commits). Empty chain when the plan has no recorded revisions yet.

guidance.when: You need a plan's edit history with the *why* — what changed at each revision and the rationale behind it. The basis of the Revisions panel and of the context an agent launched from the plan is seeded with.
guidance.notWhen: You want raw git commit history of the file — that is plans:history. The current plan body — plans:get.
guidance.chaining: plans:revisions → plans:diff for a coarse git patch, or (Phase 2) the per-revision transcript verb for the conversation behind a revision.

tools.name: plans:run-transcript
tools.description: A paginated slice of a plan run's transcript — turns ordered by seq; substring-filterable, never a whole dump. The data behind the Agents-tab run-detail view.

guidance.when: You want to inspect the back-and-forth of an existing run — e.g. find a specific turn before resuming.
guidance.notWhen: You want the run launches list (plans:runs), the conversation behind a plan revision (plans:revision-transcript), or to continue the run (plans:resume).
guidance.chaining: plans:runs → plans:run-transcript { runId } → page with cursor.

tools.name: plans:runs
tools.description: The launch history for a plan, newest-first — one row per agent launched from it: run id, title, status, who launched it and when, the launch note, the seeded content hash, the session id, and a transcript turn count. Empty list when the plan has never been launched.

guidance.when: You want to see the agents launched from a plan — the past-runs list, or to find a runId to resume.
guidance.notWhen: You want to launch a fresh agent — plans:launch. You want to read the plan body — plans:get. The plan’s edit history — plans:revisions.
guidance.chaining: plans:runs → plans:resume { runId, message } to continue a run.

tools.name: plans:search
tools.description: Search across SU plans by keyword. Scopes: title, now, items, decisions, prose. Includes archived + legacy by default.

guidance.when: You're looking for prior work, decisions, or items by topic and don't have a slug.
guidance.notWhen: You already know the slug — use plans:get. For full prose recall across the project (chats, escalations), use search:fulltext.
guidance.chaining: plans:search { query } → plans:get { slug } on the top hit.

tools.name: plans:set-content
tools.description: Replace a plan file wholesale, guarded by a compare-and-swap on `expectedHash`. For raw-prose edits the structured verbs cannot make. Rejects a stale write (file changed since load), a write that would strip a real plan back to legacy, and a write that fails lint. A successful write is recorded as a plan revision; pass `rationale` to capture the why. For large plan bodies, use plans:set-content-chunk instead so the provider sends multiple small tool calls.

guidance.when: A human is editing the raw markdown of a plan — prose sections the assisted verbs (set-now / set-status / add-decision / add-item) do not cover. Use only for small-to-medium bodies that fit comfortably in one tool call.
guidance.notWhen: A structured edit — flipping an item, replacing the Now block, appending a decision/item — use the assisted verb. Converting a legacy plan — use plans:set-frontmatter. Writing a large plan body — use plans:set-content-chunk begin → append* → commit.
guidance.chaining: plans:get { slug } → carry `contentHash` → plans:set-content { slug, content, expectedHash: contentHash }. For large bodies: plans:set-content-chunk begin → append* → commit.

tools.name: plans:set-content-chunk
tools.description: Stage a large plans:set-content rewrite through small chunks. Use begin with expectedHash, append each markdown chunk, then commit. Commit validates/lints/CAS-writes exactly like plans:set-content and records one revision. Use this instead of plans:set-content for large plan bodies that may trip provider/tool-call limits.

guidance.when: Writing or rewriting a large plan body. If the plan markdown is more than a few screens, use begin → append* → commit with chunks under 24k characters instead of sending one huge plans:set-content call.
guidance.notWhen: Small raw-prose edits — plans:set-content is simpler. Structured edits — use plans:set-now / plans:set-status / plans:add-decision / plans:add-item.
guidance.chaining: plans:get { slug } → plans:set-content-chunk { op:"begin", slug, expectedHash: contentHash, chunk:firstPart, rationale } → append remaining chunks → commit. If commit returns stale, plans:get again and restart the draft.

tools.name: plans:set-frontmatter
tools.description: Convert a legacy plan (no valid frontmatter) into a first-class plan by writing a complete `title`/`slug`/`created`/`updated`/`status`/`owner` block. Body untouched. Refuses a plan that already has valid frontmatter.

guidance.when: Promoting a legacy plan — one with no/malformed frontmatter — to a tracked plan, e.g. from the Plans admin tab triage screen.
guidance.notWhen: Editing a plan that already has valid frontmatter — that would clobber keys this verb does not model; use plans:set-content for a deliberate raw edit. Routine status flips on items use plans:set-status.
guidance.chaining: plans:list (isLegacy: true rows) → plans:set-frontmatter per plan → plans:get to confirm.

tools.name: plans:set-importance
tools.description: Change one item's importance (urgent|high|normal|low). Adds/replaces the trailing `importance:` keyword; setting `normal` removes it. Auto-bumps frontmatter updated:.

guidance.when: An item's importance changes — escalating a stuck or aging item, or correcting a level set wrong at creation.
guidance.notWhen: Setting importance when creating an item — that's plans:add-item's required arg. Changing lifecycle status — plans:set-status.
guidance.chaining: plans:items (sorted urgent→low) → plans:set-importance to re-rank what the human sees first.

tools.name: plans:set-now
tools.description: Replace the `## Now` block atomically. The Now block is the cold-resume anchor — the single most-read field. Auto-bumps frontmatter updated:.

guidance.when: Plan state advances meaningfully — phase boundaries, blocking discovery, finishing a chunk of work, picking up a new direction.
guidance.notWhen: Per-item flip — that's plans:set-status. Or a decision — that's plans:add-decision.
guidance.chaining: plans:set-status to flip current item → plans:set-now reflecting the new state.

tools.name: plans:set-plan-status
tools.description: Flip a plan's lifecycle status (draft→ready approve, ready→draft demote, →shipped, →superseded reject). Plan-level frontmatter, not an item's status. Auto-bumps updated:.

guidance.when: Moving a whole plan through its lifecycle: approving a reviewed draft (draft→ready, which unlocks Start), demoting an approved plan back to draft, shipping it, or rejecting it (→superseded).
guidance.notWhen: Flipping a P-NNN item's status — use plans:set-status. Converting a legacy plan that has no valid frontmatter — use plans:set-frontmatter first (this verb refuses it with no_status_line).
guidance.chaining: plans:get (read current status) → plans:set-plan-status { slug, status: 'ready', expectedCurrent: 'draft' } to approve. Approving is optional before plans:start — starting a draft auto-approves it (draft→ready).

tools.name: plans:set-priority
tools.description: Set the cross-plan dispatch priority for a started plan. Lower = dispatched first. The drag-to-reorder UI calls this automatically; agents can also call it when explicit ordering matters.

guidance.when: User drags a started plan to a new position in the Plans rail, or explicitly asks "do plan A before plan B".
guidance.notWhen: For pausing a plan, use plans:pause. For the run lifecycle, use plans:set-run-status.
guidance.chaining: plans:list to see started plans and their current priorities.

tools.name: plans:set-run-status
tools.description: Manually transition a plan run's status — archive it (set aside, still resumable), mark it done (deliberately concluded), or set it idle (un-archive / reopen). A run that is currently running is rejected. Distinct from plans:set-status, which is for plan items.

guidance.when: You want to archive a finished run, mark a run done, or un-archive one — a deliberate lifecycle change a human/agent makes.
guidance.notWhen: The run is mid-turn (let it settle, or resume it). Flipping a plan *item* status is plans:set-status. Continuing a run is plans:resume.
guidance.chaining: plans:runs → plans:set-run-status { runId, status }.

tools.name: plans:set-status
tools.description: Flip one item's stored status. Writes the exact bytes a human would type. Auto-bumps frontmatter updated:.

guidance.when: An item's status changes — picking up (todo→wip), completing (wip→done), gating on a human (→needs-human), or recording external blockage (→blocked).
guidance.notWhen: You want to add a brand-new item — use plans:add-item. Or to change scope of the work — edit the item text directly in the file.
guidance.chaining: plans:items { actionable: true } → plans:set-status { itemId, status: "wip" } when picking up.

tools.name: plans:start
tools.description: Mark a plan as started so the orchestrator will pick features promoted from it. Starting is itself the approval signal — a still-draft plan is auto-advanced to 'ready'. Starting an already-started plan is a no-op. Use plans:pause to suspend work without losing started state.

guidance.when: User clicks 'Start Plan' in the harness UI, or an agent is asked to begin work on a specific plan.
guidance.notWhen: The plan is already started. Use plans:pause to suspend, plans:set-run-status for run lifecycle.
guidance.chaining: plans:list to find the slug, then plans:start { slug }.

tools.name: plans:summarize-revision
tools.description: Fill in a revision's missing rationale by summarising the conversation behind it on the haiku model. Best-effort and idempotent — a revision that already has a rationale, or has no plan-run transcript, is reported back unchanged.

guidance.when: A revision from a plan-run session has no rationale and you want the "why" filled in — for the Revisions panel or a richer launch-context digest.
guidance.notWhen: The revision already has a rationale. The revision is a direct editor save or a git backfill (no conversation to summarise).
guidance.chaining: plans:revisions (spot a rationale-less row) → plans:summarize-revision { revisionId }.

tools.name: plugins:fire_event
tools.description: Fire a free-form plugin event or typed lifecycle hook via the in-process host. Diagnostic — architect/operator only.

guidance.when: Synthetically fire a hook event so the registered plugin / role pipelines run their handlers. Useful for replaying / testing event-driven flows.
guidance.notWhen: For NORMAL flow, events fire from real actions (commit, plan-approved, etc.); only use this when you need to manually trigger them. For listing PENDING events, use `pending_events:list`.

tools.name: plugins:invoke_action
tools.description: Invoke a plugin action via the in-process registry. Diagnostic — architect/operator only.

guidance.when: Invoke a named action a plugin exposes (publish, sync, etc.). Use the action name from `plugins:runtime_status`.
guidance.notWhen: For TOOLS the plugin exposes (callable as MCP names), call them directly via their mcp__ prefix. Actions are plugin-lifecycle verbs; tools are the catalog.

tools.name: plugins:runtime_status
tools.description: Read the plugin host runtime status (loaded plugins, registered actions, mounted api routes).

guidance.when: You need to know which plugins are loaded + healthy in the current operator process (per-harness or workspace-level).
guidance.notWhen: For the plugin CATALOG (everything installable), use the marketplace endpoints. plugins:runtime_status is the runtime view.

tools.name: plugins:tui_panes
tools.description: List the capability-gated tui-pane UI contributions for a harness (pluginName, slug, label, command, cwd). The pui opens these in a zellij pane.

guidance.when: The pui (or an agent) needs the TUI panes (type:'tui-pane' UI contributions) a harness's enabled plugins offer, to open one in a terminal pane.
guidance.notWhen: For desktop UI surfaces (react/iframe) or the full plugin runtime status, use plugins:runtime_status.

tools.name: pot:declare-wake
tools.description: Declare the Pot operator's next wake (REPLACE semantics — omitted parts are cleared): a time (`at` ISO / `inSeconds`), event subscriptions (`events: [{on, when?, note?}]`), both, or nothing (`mode:'none'`). The time is clamped to a wake floor; event wakes fire pot:wake when the subscribed tool-event matches.

guidance.when: You are the pot/operator ending a turn — ALWAYS declare your next wake (a time, events, or explicitly none). Also when the user asks to schedule or re-schedule the operator.
guidance.notWhen: To fire the pot right now — that is pot:wake.
guidance.chaining: pot:status to inspect the current declaration; pot:wake for an immediate manual fire.

tools.name: pot:status
tools.description: The Pot operator's current wake declaration: the pending time wake (one-shot routine), event subscriptions + live rule ids, last wake, and the floor. Read-only.

guidance.when: To see when/whether the operator will wake next, or to verify a pot:declare-wake landed.
guidance.chaining: pot:declare-wake to change the declaration; pot:wake to fire now.

tools.name: pot:wake
tools.description: Fire the Pot operator immediately (launches the pot blueprint via the invoke route). Floor-debounced: a wake within the floor window of the previous one is skipped unless force:true. The target of event-wake reaction rules and the manual user override.

guidance.when: The user asks to wake/kick the operator now, or an event-wake rule fires (it targets this tool automatically).
guidance.notWhen: To schedule a future wake — that is pot:declare-wake.
guidance.chaining: pot:status to see the last/next wake; pot:declare-wake to schedule.

tools.name: processes:kill
tools.description:
When to use: User says "kill that process", "stop the runaway harness" — sends SIGTERM (then SIGKILL after timeout) to a tracked OS process.

When NOT to use: For SPAWNED agents, use `orchestrator.cancel`. For DELEGATES, use the delegate-cancel endpoint. processes:kill is the OS-level escape hatch.

guidance.when: User says "kill that process", "stop the runaway harness" — sends SIGTERM (then SIGKILL after timeout) to a tracked OS process.
guidance.notWhen: For SPAWNED agents, use `orchestrator.cancel`. For DELEGATES, use the delegate-cancel endpoint. processes:kill is the OS-level escape hatch.

tools.name: projects:get
tools.description: Fetch a single project detail (spec, feature counts, last spec revision summary). Returns null when not found.

guidance.when: User names a specific project and wants its full record (spec, status, metadata).
guidance.notWhen: For SPEC revisions / history, use `projects:spec_revisions`. For the runtime harness state, use `harness:get`.
guidance.chaining: Follow `projects:list` for the slug.

tools.name: projects:list
tools.description: List projects relevant to a harness (filtered to those with at least one feature in the given slug). Includes feature counts.

guidance.when: User asks "what projects do I have?" or you need a project id before calling `projects:get`. Workspace-level project enumeration.
guidance.notWhen: For HARNESSES (work running inside a project), use `harness:list`. Projects ⊇ harnesses; the slug overlap is intentional but the surfaces are different.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `projects:get` for detail, or `projects:spec_revisions` for the spec history.

tools.name: projects:spec_revision
tools.description: Fetch one project spec-revision in full (includes the spec body). Returns null when not found.

guidance.when: User names a specific revision id and wants its full body — what the spec looked like at that point.
guidance.notWhen: For the CURRENT spec, use `projects:get`. For the list of revisions, use `projects:spec_revisions`.
guidance.chaining: Follow `projects:spec_revisions` for the id.

tools.name: projects:spec_revisions
tools.description: List spec-revision summaries for a project (newest-first; full spec body lives on projects:spec_revision).

guidance.when: User asks "how has the spec changed?", "when did we update X?", or you need a list of spec revision ids before reading one.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE revision's body, use `projects:spec_revision`. For the current spec, use `projects:get`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `projects:spec_revision` to read a specific revision.

tools.name: rationale:feed
tools.description: The "why" of a subsystem-topic: the decisions, work-items, and insights relevant to it, projected from the plans/work-items/insights — indexed, no full search, never stale. Each entry carries a `ref` to drill into via plans:get / docs:get.

guidance.when: Before working in a subsystem (e.g. `coordination-substrate`), to load the rationale behind it — why it is the way it is — without searching everything.
guidance.notWhen: You want the cross-object work-stream / status of an area (topics:feed), the list of topics (topics:list), or messages waiting for you (coord:inbox).
guidance.chaining: topics:list → rationale:feed { topic } → plans:get / docs:get on an entry’s `ref` for the full text.

tools.name: rationale:reproject
tools.description: Re-derive a source (plan / work-item / insight) into the topic-keyed rationale index, or backfill all of them. Idempotent. Normally fired automatically by the event engine; call directly to backfill (kind:"all") or force a resync.

guidance.when: To backfill the rationale index (kind:"all") on a fresh DB, or force-resync one source after an out-of-band change. Routine maintenance is automatic.
guidance.notWhen: To READ the projection — that is rationale:feed.

tools.name: roles:firing_on
tools.description: Return role manifests whose `firesOn` array includes the given hook event.

guidance.when: You need to know which roles are configured to fire on a given hook event before firing it (avoids no-op fires).
guidance.notWhen: For the hook-event ENUM itself, use `hooks:known`. For role details, use `roles:get`.

tools.name: roles:get
tools.description: Fetch one role manifest by id, scoped to a harness slug (or global when slug omitted).

guidance.when: User names a specific role and wants its full definition (system prompt, allowed tools, quotas).
guidance.notWhen: For the role list, use `roles:list`. For the known-role enum (static), use `roles:known`.

tools.name: roles:known
tools.description: Static well-known role-id allowlist (kernel set; plugin-registered roles extend this).

guidance.when: Static enum of role names the runtime supports — use to validate a role string before passing it elsewhere.
guidance.notWhen: For the workspace's ACTUAL roles (may be a subset), use `roles:list`. known is the universe; list is what's configured.

tools.name: roles:list
tools.description: List role manifests (id, source, fires-on, etc.) for a harness, or globally when no harness given.

guidance.when: You need the set of agent roles configured in the workspace (architect, worker, validator, …) before spawning or dispatching.
guidance.notWhen: For agents currently RUNNING, use `agents:list`. roles:list is the static configuration; agents:list is the live processes.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `roles:get` for one role's definition.

tools.name: saved_prompts:list
tools.description: List cross-client saved prompts for a scope: omit harness_slug for workspace-global prompts, or pass a harness slug for that harness. Returns the canonical PG rows (name, body, description, arg_hint) that materialize to the /name slash-commands in Claude / Codex / OMP.

guidance.when: When you need to inspect which saved `/name` prompts exist for a workspace or harness (e.g. to answer "what prompts are defined?" or before suggesting one).
guidance.notWhen: To create/edit/delete a prompt — that is the dashboard settings UI (POST /api/agent-mcp/saved-prompts). This tool is read-only.

tools.name: search:fulltext
tools.description: Search workspace prose (escalations, brainstorm notes, older operator turns) by keyword match (BM25-style). Ranked by relevance. Returns excerpts.

guidance.when: User references prose past the chat history budget ("remember when we decided pricing", "the X discussion from last week"), or asks about content in escalations/brainstorm where the right SQL filter is not obvious. Returns ranked snippets.
guidance.notWhen: For STRUCTURED queries on harness state, features, tasks, issues, or messages — use the dedicated tools (harness:status, tasks:list, etc). They are faster and more precise when the schema matches the query. For CODE recall, use `gitnexus:query`. For tasks/goals/projects text, use `search:query`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `harness:escalation` or `harness:plan_reviews` to fetch the full row of a returned hit. The result `excerpt` is just the first 200 chars for ranking display.

tools.name: search:query
tools.description:
When to use: User asks an open-ended question that could match anything in the workspace ("anything about auth?", "find references to budget guard"). Cross-resource full-text search over tasks, goals, projects, audit, messages.

When NOT to use: For a SPECIFIC resource type, use the dedicated list/get tool — search is broader but ranked less precisely. For code-graph queries, use `gitnexus:query`.

guidance.when: User asks an open-ended question that could match anything in the workspace ("anything about auth?", "find references to budget guard"). Cross-resource full-text search over tasks, goals, projects, audit, messages.
guidance.notWhen: For a SPECIFIC resource type, use the dedicated list/get tool — search is broader but ranked less precisely. For code-graph queries, use `gitnexus:query`.

tools.name: search:semantic
tools.description: Semantic recall over workspace prose using embedding similarity. mode=hybrid combines with BM25 (search:fulltext) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion for best of both keyword and meaning. Falls back to BM25 if embeddings unavailable.

guidance.when: User asks about a concept by paraphrase rather than the exact keyword used in the recorded text. Examples: "when did we talk about authentication strategy" (could match "login flow", "auth approach", "JWT decision"). Prefer mode=hybrid for best recall.
guidance.notWhen: When the user knows the exact keyword they want. `search:fulltext` is faster + cheaper there (no embedding API call). For structured queries (tasks/goals/projects rows by title), use `search:query`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `harness:escalation` or `harness:plan_reviews` to fetch the full row of a hit.

tools.name: snapshots:get
tools.description: Fetch one snapshot listing by id. Returns null when not in the registry.

guidance.when: User names a specific snapshot id and wants its full content (spec, code, history).
guidance.notWhen: For the snapshot list, use `snapshots:list` first.
guidance.chaining: Follow `snapshots:list` for the id.

tools.name: snapshots:list
tools.description: List every published snapshot known to the workspace registry (id, slug, version, …).

guidance.when: User asks "what snapshots do I have?", "any backups?". Cross-harness snapshot enumeration.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE snapshot's detail, use `snapshots:get`. For automated backups (not snapshots), check backup-group tools.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `snapshots:get` for content.

tools.name: substrate:revoke_contributor
tools.description: OWNER action: revoke another contributor from a shared harness by adding their device pubkeys to the harness revocation set (revoked_pubkeys). Every peer honors it on the next admission re-verify and drops them from live federation. Requires repo-admin token.

guidance.when: OWNER action: revoke ANOTHER contributor by adding their device pubkeys to the harness revocation set (requires repo-admin token). Every peer drops them on its next admission re-verify. Use when a contributor is a confirmed bad actor, their account is compromised, or they must be removed from the shared harness's federation entirely.
guidance.notWhen: Revoking your OWN device — use `substrate:revoke_self_device` instead. Also not when the token does not have GitHub admin permissions on the shared repo.
guidance.chaining: Resolve the contributor's githubUserId from the Contributors tab, `dev:dogfood_substrate_status`, or `harness:membership` first — githubUserId is the stable numeric GitHub user id, not the login.

tools.name: substrate:revoke_self_device
tools.description: Revoke one of your own device pubkeys from a harness (lost or rotated device). Adds the pubkey to revoked_pubkeys in your contributor row, replicates to peers, and drops the device from the booted substrate immediately.

guidance.when: Revoke ONE of your OWN device keys from a harness (a lost or rotated device) so peers stop admitting it.
guidance.notWhen: Revoking ANOTHER contributor's key / kicking out a bad actor — not supported (self-revocation only, v2 for owner-revocation).
guidance.chaining: Resolve the device pubkey from the contributor's own device_attestations first (e.g. via dev:dogfood_substrate_status or the Contributors tab).

tools.name: tasks:create
tools.description:
When to use: User asks to add a task / TODO / item to track. Always confirm the title out loud before calling — task creation isn't silent.

When NOT to use: For asking the harness to DO work (write code, run validation), use `<spawn role="worker" />` instead — tasks track intent, spawns execute it.

Chaining: After creating, mention the task id in your reply so the user can refer back.

guidance.when: User asks to add a task / TODO / item to track. Always confirm the title out loud before calling — task creation isn't silent.
guidance.notWhen: For asking the harness to DO work (write code, run validation), use `<spawn role="worker" />` instead — tasks track intent, spawns execute it.
guidance.chaining: After creating, mention the task id in your reply so the user can refer back.

tools.name: tasks:get
tools.description:
When to use: User names a specific task ("the auth task", "task ABC-123") and you need its full body.

When NOT to use: For a list of tasks, use `tasks:list` first. Don't call `tasks:get` speculatively across many ids — list returns enough for most "what's the gist" questions.

Chaining: Follow `tasks:list` to find the id.

guidance.when: User names a specific task ("the auth task", "task ABC-123") and you need its full body.
guidance.notWhen: For a list of tasks, use `tasks:list` first. Don't call `tasks:get` speculatively across many ids — list returns enough for most "what's the gist" questions.
guidance.chaining: Follow `tasks:list` to find the id.

tools.name: tasks:list
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what tasks do I have?", "what's on my plate", or you need a task id before calling `tasks:get`/`tasks:update`/`tasks:close`.

When NOT to use: For ONE task by id, use `tasks:get`. For creating a task, use `tasks:create`. For PROJECTS / FEATURES (work the harness is doing), use `harness:*` — tasks are separate from harness features.

Chaining: Pair with `tasks:get` for detail on a specific row.

guidance.when: User asks "what tasks do I have?", "what's on my plate", or you need a task id before calling `tasks:get`/`tasks:update`/`tasks:close`.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE task by id, use `tasks:get`. For creating a task, use `tasks:create`. For PROJECTS / FEATURES (work the harness is doing), use `harness:*` — tasks are separate from harness features.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `tasks:get` for detail on a specific row.

tools.name: topics:create
tools.description: Create a coordination topic: a short slug + one-sentence description. Prefer an existing topic (topics:list) over a near-duplicate. Notifies new_topic subscribers; re-creating an existing slug is a no-op.

guidance.when: No existing topic fits a relevance area you (and likely others) will want to follow. Keep the slug to a word or two; the description to one sentence.
guidance.notWhen: A close-enough topic already exists in topics:list — subscribe/tag to that instead. Near-duplicates get merged with topics:merge.

tools.name: topics:feed
tools.description: Read everything tagged with a topic — across issues, conversations, features, and plans — the whole work-stream of an area. Each item carries its title + current state.

guidance.when: To understand all current work in a relevance area before you start in it, or to see what is happening with e.g. `zero-cache` across every object kind.
guidance.notWhen: You want messages waiting for you (coord:inbox) or just the list of topics (topics:list).
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:feed { topic } → issues:get / conversations:get on an item.

tools.name: topics:list
tools.description: List coordination topics (tag + one-sentence description) and your own active topic subscriptions. A topic = a relevance area you can follow to have its updates injected into your context.

guidance.when: At the start of work, to see the shared topic taxonomy before tagging/subscribing — and to prefer an existing topic over creating a near-duplicate (D-004).
guidance.notWhen: You want the messages already waiting for you — that is coord:inbox, not this.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:subscribe (follow a relevant area) or topics:create (only if nothing fits).

tools.name: topics:merge
tools.description: Merge topic `from` into `into`: aliases the slug (tags resolve to the target) and re-points the merged topic’s subscribers onto the target. The dedup for accidental near-duplicate topics.

guidance.when: topics:list shows two topics that mean the same thing — fold the lesser-used into the better one.
guidance.notWhen: The two topics are genuinely distinct areas — keep both.

tools.name: topics:subscribe
tools.description: Subscribe to a topic so its updates are injected into your inbox — the named sugar for watch(topic,{wake:false}). mode = full | digest | mention (D-006 noise tiering). Subscribe to the built-in `new_topic` to learn of new topics as they appear. Idempotent — re-subscribing updates the mode/TTL.

guidance.when: A topic in topics:list is relevant to your current work and you want its updates pushed to you. Pick digest for high-churn areas, mention to stay quiet.
guidance.notWhen: You only need a one-time look — just topics:list. To follow a specific object (one thread/issue), that is the object’s own subscribe, not a topic.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:subscribe; topics:unsubscribe to stop.

tools.name: topics:tag
tools.description: Tag a coordination object (issue / conversation / feature / plan) with a topic so it appears in that topic's feed and its changes reach the topic's subscribers. Pass remove:true to untag.

guidance.when: You want a feature/plan/issue/conversation to be visible to everyone following a relevance area — tag it with the topic.
guidance.notWhen: The topic does not exist yet — topics:create it first (prefer an existing one). For an issue you can also use issues:tag.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:tag { object_kind, object_ref, topic } → topics:feed { topic }.

tools.name: topics:unsubscribe
tools.description: Unsubscribe from a topic. Idempotent — unsubscribing from a topic you do not follow is a no-op.

guidance.when: A topic you followed is no longer relevant and its updates are noise.
guidance.notWhen: You want to mute briefly — set the subscription to mention mode via topics:subscribe instead of dropping it.

tools.name: tui:dispatch
tools.description: Dispatch a control intent to a running pui (terminal workbench) and wait for the result. Built-in intents: get_state ({}) → snapshot of the pui AppState (active tab, selections, counts, chat state, live panes); set_tab ({tab:"Operator"|"Plans"|"Sessions"|"Fleet"|…}); set_harness ({slug}); select ({list:"plans"|"roster"|"inbox"|"features"|"issues"|"docs", index}); open_chat ({}) → focus the operator chat pane; focus_pane ({pane_id}) → focus a worker's zellij pane (ids from get_state.panes). client_id targets the pui instance (its workbench owner key, $USER@$HOSTNAME by default).

guidance.when: You need to drive or read a running pui terminal workbench — switch its tab, change its active harness, move a selection, or read its current state. Side-effect tool: writes a tui_intents row the pui consumes over SSE.
guidance.notWhen: For the browser/desktop UI use `ui:dispatch`. For showing a question + choices use `chat:ask_choice`. For delegating work use `<spawn>` — tui:dispatch is UI control, not work delegation.

tools.name: ui:dispatch
tools.description: Dispatch a UI intent to a browser tab and wait for the result. Defaults client_id to ctx.uiClientId (the tab that spawned the agent). Built-in intents: set_url ({params:{...}}), snapshot ({selector?,mode?}), read_visible_text, focus, scroll_into_view, click. Pages can register additional intents via useUiIntent(name, handler).

guidance.when: You need to make something happen in the user's browser tab — open the panel, navigate, focus a card, etc. Side-effect tool: writes a ui_intents row the tab consumes via SSE.
guidance.notWhen: For showing a question + choices in the chat, use `chat:ask_choice` (renders inline buttons). For asking the operator brain to delegate work, use `<spawn>` — `ui:dispatch` is for UI side effects, not work delegation.

tools.name: ui:get_state
tools.description: Read the URL state of a browser tab (defaults to the tab that spawned the agent via ctx.uiClientId). Returns { url, pathname, params, title, last_seen_at }. Use to answer "what is the user looking at?" — nuqs serializes panel/tab/filter/selection state to the URL, so the params object reflects most UI state.

guidance.when: User asks "what am I looking at?", "what page am I on?", or you need to verify a panel state before acting ("is the panel already open?").
guidance.notWhen: Tool calls ARE idempotent — `panel_open` when already open is fine. Don't pre-check just to skip a call; the persona rule is "always call". Use `ui:get_state` only when you need to BRANCH on what the user is looking at.

tools.name: ui:list_clients
tools.description: List open browser tabs (UI clients) with active presence. Each entry is { client_id, workspace_id, url, title, last_seen_at, opened_at, is_self }. is_self=true when the client matches ctx.uiClientId (i.e., the tab that spawned the agent).

guidance.when: You need to know which browser tab(s) the user has open before calling `ui:dispatch`. Returns client ids the operator can target.
guidance.notWhen: In the operator-converse path, ctx.uiClientId is already populated — you can target the user's current tab directly via `ui:dispatch`. Only list when you need to choose between multiple tabs.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `ui:get_state` to see what each tab is on, then `ui:dispatch` to act.

tools.name: voice:agent
tools.description: Voice agent peer: toggle channel listening (STT) or the converse BRAIN (auto-reply), report status, or speak text (TTS) into the active channel.

guidance.when: Toggle the agent's ears ({op:'enable'|'disable'}), its auto-reply brain ({op:'brain', on}), read {op:'status'}, or speak into the channel ({op:'say', text}).
guidance.notWhen: Joining/leaving the channel itself is `voice:join`/`voice:leave`; this controls only the agent's listen/think/speak behaviors on top.
guidance.chaining: voice:join → voice:agent {op:'brain', on:true} (ears + auto-reply: peer speech → operator-converse → spoken reply). For manual control use {op:'enable'} then {op:'say', text:'…'}.

tools.name: voice:channels
tools.description: List/create/remove P2P voice channels (the durable registry; a channel maps a name to a swarm topic).

guidance.when: Manage the voice-channel registry — list what channels exist, create one before joining it, or remove a stale one.
guidance.notWhen: To enter/exit a channel use `voice:join` / `voice:leave`; for who's in a channel right now use `voice:status`.
guidance.chaining: voice:channels {op:'create'} → voice:join {channel} → voice:status.

tools.name: voice:join
tools.description: Join a P2P voice channel by id or name — starts the voice swarm, announces the topic, connects to peers.

guidance.when: Enter a voice channel (by id or name from `voice:channels`). One active channel at a time; joining another leaves the current one.
guidance.notWhen: Don't poll this — `voice:status` reads the live state; the local voice socket pushes status events to UI clients.
guidance.chaining: voice:channels {op:'list'} → voice:join → speak via the local voice socket (pui/desktop) → voice:leave.

tools.name: voice:leave
tools.description: Leave the active P2P voice channel (drops peer connections, releases the swarm topic).

guidance.when: Exit the current voice channel. Safe no-op when not in one.
guidance.notWhen: Removing a channel from the registry is `voice:channels {op:'remove'}` — leaving only ends THIS node's participation.

tools.name: voice:status
tools.description: Live voice state: active channel, mute, and in-channel peers (id/label/muted/speaking).

guidance.when: Read who's in the active voice channel right now (presence is in-band — liveness IS the peer connection).
guidance.notWhen: The durable channel LIST is `voice:channels {op:'list'}` — status only covers the channel this node is in.

tools.name: watch:create
tools.description: The unified subscription primitive — watch(pattern, {wake, once, min_sleep_sec, urgency, timeout_sec, mode}): register an interest, receive a delivery. DELIVERY — wake:false (DEFAULT, cheap) injects updates into your coord inbox (seen on your next natural turn, no token cost); wake:true (opt-in, a turn = tokens) re-invokes you when it fires. CARDINALITY — once:true is one-shot (fires once, auto-consumes — a grant/readiness); once:false is standing (re-fires on every match). Named sugar presets: `events:await {key}` = watch(key,{wake:true,once:true}); `topics:subscribe {topic}` = watch(topic,{wake:false}). Lifecycle: events:cancel / events:status (wake) · topics:unsubscribe (inject).

guidance.when: Register interest in something and receive its updates. Prefer wake:false (inject) for continuous awareness of a churning area — no cost. Use wake:true ONLY for specific readiness ("wake me when THIS grant/lock/deadline is ready"); for a standing wake watch set min_sleep_sec to bound the re-wake rate. once:true for a one-shot grant; once:false to keep following.
guidance.notWhen: A sub-minute wait inside one turn — just do the bounded blocking call. A recurring TIME schedule — the pot/routines own time-based wakes. Ambient interest where a wake would burn turns — use wake:false.
guidance.chaining: wake:true → end your turn; on wake the turn text carries the event + payload. events:cancel (wake) / topics:unsubscribe (inject) to stop; events:status to inspect your active wake watches + recent wakes.

tools.name: wiki:backlinks
tools.description: Find markdown files that reference [[target]] across the workspace. Returns { target, harness, hits[] }.

guidance.when: User asks "what links to X?", "where is `[[name]]` referenced?". Wiki-style backlink lookup across markdown files.
guidance.notWhen: For cross-resource full-text search, use `search:query`. For markdown TOC, use `harness:markdown_index`.

tools.name: work_items:claim
tools.description: Claim a work-item (assign it to yourself, or to `assignee`). Claiming a feature sets taken_by; an issue sets assignee.

guidance.when: You are starting work on a work-item — claim it so peers do not duplicate.
guidance.chaining: work_items:list → work_items:claim → work_items:set_state → work_items:release/close.

tools.name: work_items:claim_next
tools.description: Self-select: atomically claim the OLDEST unclaimed work-item in a harness (tuple-space `in` via SKIP LOCKED + work-stealing). Competing agents never double-claim. Returns the claimed item or null.

guidance.when: You are an idle agent picking up work — prefer this self-selection over waiting to be assigned. Returns the oldest claimable feature-family item, now yours.
guidance.notWhen: When a SPECIFIC item must go to a SPECIFIC agent — that is work_items:claim with an explicit assignee (named assignment, the exception).
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim_next → work_items:set_state → work_items:release.

tools.name: work_items:comment
tools.description: Comment on a work-item (any kind). Appends to its thread and notifies subscribers. The thread is created on the first comment.

guidance.when: You have an update, a finding, or a question on a work-item that its followers should see.
guidance.chaining: work_items:get → work_items:comment; work_items:subscribe to follow the thread.

tools.name: work_items:complete
tools.description: Finish a work-item with a STRUCTURED completion record (what landed / migrations / tests / deferred-set) instead of a hand-written coord:send prose dump. The system renders + broadcasts the completion notification from the fields — you spend no tokens narrating. Optionally also transitions the item to a terminal `state`. Returns a `reflect` step (the self-learning friction prompt) to act on once, now.

guidance.when: You finished a work-item / plan-item / brief. Fill in the structured completion fields (summary, whatLanded, migrations, tests, deferred) — do NOT also coord:send a prose summary; this emits it.
guidance.notWhen: For a contextual aside that is not a completion (a question, a design note), use coord:send. To only change state without a completion record, use work_items:set_state.
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim → … → work_items:complete { id, completion }. The completion auto-emits to coord:inbox; no coord:send needed. Then read the returned `reflect` step (self-learning loop): if any friction marker bit you during this unit of work, file it once via improvements:capture — else capture nothing.

tools.name: work_items:create
tools.description: Create a work-item of any kind — feature | research-task | chunk | bug | change. Returns a kind-independent WI-NNN id. bug/change file a tracked issue; feature/research-task/chunk enter the harness work queue (feature/research-task pickable by the pipeline; chunk is an execution sub-unit carrying a parent). Dedup with work_items:list/search first.

guidance.when: You want to track a unit of work an agent will do. Pick the kind: bug (something broken), change (a desired one-off / DX ask), feature (a pipeline work-unit), research-task, or chunk (a sub-unit of a parent, pass `parent`).
guidance.notWhen: A passing question with no owner → coord:ask. A validator finding inside a live pipeline run → the validator pipeline, not here.
guidance.chaining: work_items:list (dedup) → work_items:create → work_items:claim when you start → work_items:set_state on progress; work_items:promote to give a bug/change a pipeline run.

tools.name: work_items:get
tools.description: Fetch one work-item by id (WI-/F-/EI-…) across every kind. Pass `harness` to disambiguate a feature id that may repeat across harnesses.

guidance.when: You have a work-item id and need its full state (kind, lifecycle, assignee, parent).
guidance.chaining: work_items:list → work_items:get { id } for detail.

tools.name: work_items:link
tools.description: Link this work-item to a target (rel: blocks | relates | duplicates | fixes). Blocking works across kinds. Target = another work-item (target_id) or an explicit coord ref (target_kind + target_ref, e.g. a plan_item). Pass remove:true to unlink.

guidance.when: You discovered a dependency/relationship: this work-item blocks/relates-to/duplicates/fixes another work-item or plan item.
guidance.chaining: work_items:get both sides → work_items:link { rel:"blocks", target_id }.

tools.name: work_items:list
tools.description: List work-items across kinds (feature/research-task/chunk/bug/change). Default shows top-level items (chunks are hidden — pass parent or includeChildren). Filter by harness, kind, state. Returns the WorkItem array directly.

guidance.when: You want the current work-items in a harness (or operator-wide). Default hides chunks; pass `parent` to see a parent's chunks.
guidance.chaining: work_items:list → work_items:get { id } for detail; work_items:claim to take one.

tools.name: work_items:observe
tools.description: Observe a work-item WITHOUT claiming it (tuple-space `rd`): reports availability + who holds it. Distinct from claim (`in`).

guidance.when: Inspect a work-item's claimability before deciding to claim it — read without taking.
guidance.chaining: work_items:observe → work_items:claim (if available).

tools.name: work_items:promote
tools.description: Promote a bug/change work-item into a feature pipeline run (mints an F-FIX feature in the target harness and links it). An operator-scope item needs an explicit harness.

guidance.when: A filed bug/change is ready to be worked by the pipeline.
guidance.notWhen: It is a passing idea (leave it filed) or already a feature.
guidance.chaining: work_items:create { kind:"bug" } → work_items:promote { harness } → the pipeline picks up the feature.

tools.name: work_items:release
tools.description: Release a work-item (clear its assignee / taken_by) so another agent can pick it up.

guidance.when: You claimed a work-item but are no longer working it.
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim → … → work_items:release.

tools.name: work_items:reorder
tools.description: Move a work-item to a position (`rank`, 0-based, 0 = head-of-line) within its assignee's ordered work-list — peers shift down to make room. This is the externalized per-agent queue the Queen reads for placement decisions. `writer`='bee' (default) for a bee resequencing its own list; `writer`='queen' for a Queen overlay (inject/rebalance) — the propose/dispose audit.

guidance.when: You are a bee resequencing your own work-list (move a just-discovered task up, push a blocked one down) OR the Queen injecting/rebalancing a bee's queue. Claim the item first — rank is per-assignee.
guidance.notWhen: You only want to START an item (work_items:claim) or change its lifecycle state (work_items:set_state). Reorder changes ORDER, not ownership or state.
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim (take it) → work_items:reorder (place it in your list) → fleet:assignments { agent } to see the ordered queue. The Queen: fleet:assignments (read load + head-of-line) → work_items:reorder { writer:"queen" }.

tools.name: work_items:search
tools.description: Full-text search work-items across kinds (feature/research-task/chunk/bug/change). Matches title + body/summary. Filter by harness or kind. Use to dedup before creating.

guidance.when: You want to find existing work-items by free text (e.g. dedup before filing, or locate a known issue/feature).
guidance.chaining: work_items:search (dedup) → work_items:create, or → work_items:get { id } for detail.

tools.name: work_items:set_state
tools.description: Set a work-item's lifecycle state. feature-family: a feature status (todo|in_progress|passed|failing|deprecated…). issue-family: open|resolved|closed.

guidance.when: You moved a work-item along its lifecycle (started, resolved, etc.).
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim → … → work_items:set_state { state }.

tools.name: work_items:subscribe
tools.description: Subscribe to a work-item so its updates fan out to your inbox (mode: full | digest | mention).

guidance.when: You want to follow a work-item you do not own (e.g. one that blocks yours).
guidance.chaining: work_items:get → work_items:subscribe.

tools.name: work_items:tag
tools.description: Tag a work-item with a topic (or untag with remove:true). Routes the work-item to that topic's subscribers.

guidance.when: You want a work-item visible to agents following an area (topics:list to see topics).
guidance.chaining: topics:list → work_items:tag { topic }.
